tools.name: edit-design
tools.description:
Edit a single page within an editing transaction and/or finalize the transaction (commit or cancel). One tool covers all three actions via the `finalize` parameter.

## Modes
- **Edit** (`finalize: "keep_open"`, the default) — pass `operations` to apply edits to a page. Returns `status: "edits_unverified"` with the after-thumbnail and per-operation results.
- **Commit** (`finalize: "commit"`) — permanently save ALL changes. IRREVERSIBLE. Call with `operations` omitted (or an empty array `[]`). Returns `status: "committed"`.
- **Cancel** (`finalize: "cancel"`) — discard ALL changes and close the transaction. Call with `operations` omitted (or an empty array `[]`). Returns `status: "cancelled"`.

## IMPORTANT: editing and finalizing are separate calls
You CANNOT combine `operations` with `finalize: "commit"` or `"cancel"`. Apply and VALIDATE your edits first (compare thumbnails + inspect the returned `document`), then call again with `operations` omitted (or empty) to commit or cancel.

## How to edit
1. Call `read-design` with `open_transaction: true` to see the current page state and locator_ids, and to get the `transaction_id`.
2. Request the page thumbnail from `read-design` (`filter.fields: ["thumbnails"]`) FIRST to capture the before-thumbnail.
3. Build your operations array targeting elements by their locator_id (used as element_id).
4. Pass operations to this tool with `finalize: "keep_open"` (or omit `finalize`).

## Available operations
`update_title`, `replace_text`, `update_fill`, `insert_fill`, `delete_element`, `find_and_replace_text`, `position_element`, `resize_element`, `format_text`, `add_text`, `insert_shape`, `replace_shape`, `add_page`, `update_opacity`, `layer_element`, `recolor_element`, `rotate_element`, `group_elements`, `ungroup_elements`, `flip_media`, `crop_media`, `reorder_page`, `replace_speaker_notes`, `update_text_anchoring`, `update_stroke_properties`, `update_line_properties`, `update_autofill_field`.

## After each edit (MANDATORY)
1. Compare the before-thumbnail (from `read-design`) against the after-thumbnail returned here.
2. Inspect the `document` returned in this response to confirm updated element values and locator_ids.
3. Only after both steps may you apply corrective edits or move to the next page.

## Responsive pages
Pages with `is_responsive: true` only support: `update_title`, `replace_text`, `update_fill`, `delete_element`, `find_and_replace_text`. Other operations will be rejected. For text replacement on responsive pages, use `find_and_replace_text` (preferred) or `replace_text` only when the target element is empty. No thumbnail is returned for responsive-page edits — validate by inspecting the returned `document`.

## Before committing
Once the thumbnail looks correct, present it to the user and ask for their approval before calling this tool with `finalize: "commit"`.

tools.description:

Generate professionally designed content in Canva including visual designs (posters, social media posts, flyers) and text-based documents (memos, articles, newsletters, proposals, reports, business plans, requirements documents).

Use this tool when the user asks you to write, create, generate, or draft ANY document or visual design. Examples:
    - "Write a memo..." → use this tool to create a Canva Doc
    - "Generate a business proposal..." → use this tool to create a Canva Doc
    - "Draft a product overview..." → use this tool to create a Canva Doc

⚠️ DO NOT use this tool when the user's message contains a URL and their intent is to create a design FROM that URL — use import-design-from-url instead.

Use the 'query' parameter to tell AI what you want to create.
The tool doesn't have context of previous requests. ALWAYS include details from previous queries for each iteration.
The tool provides best results with detailed context. ALWAYS look up the chat history and provide as much context as possible in the 'query' parameter.
Ask for more details when the tool returns this error message 'Common queries will not be generated'.
The generated designs are design candidates for users to select from.
Ask for a preferred design and use 'create-design-from-candidate' tool to add the design to users' account.

tools.name: generate-design-structured
tools.description:
Generate a structured presentation design from a user-reviewed and approved outline.

⚠️ HARD REQUIREMENT:
- This tool MUST ONLY be called AFTER request-outline-review has been called AND the user has reviewed and approved the outline in the widget UI.
- This requirement applies regardless of how complete or detailed the user's original request or supplied outline is.
- If there is no approved outline from the widget, DO NOT call this tool.

If the user's message contains a URL and their intent is to create a design FROM that URL, DO NOT use this tool — use import-design-from-url instead.

DO NOT USE THIS TOOL IF:
- The user has not yet seen the outline review widget.
- The user has not approved the outline.
- The user is still requesting changes to the outline structure (e.g., "remove page 3", "add a slide about X", "change the order").
In all of these cases, you MUST call request-outline-review instead with the updated outline.

⚠️ CRITICAL - HANDLING OUTLINE MODIFICATION REQUESTS:
If the user asks to modify the outline in any way (add, remove, reorder, or change pages), you MUST:
1. Update the outline according to their request
2. Call request-outline-review again with the modified outline
3. Wait for the user to approve the new outline
4. DO NOT call this tool (generate-design-structured) until the modified outline is approved

Examples of requests that require calling request-outline-review:
- "Remove pages 6-8"
- "Add a slide about marketing strategy"
- "Change the order of slides 2 and 3"
- "Make it shorter"
- Any other request to modify the outline structure or content

PURPOSE:
- Generate a Canva presentation design using the finalized outline that was reviewed and approved by the user.
- Convert the approved outline into a fully structured presentation design.

WHEN TO USE:
- AFTER the outline review flow is complete AND one of the following is true:
  - The user clicks the "Generate Design" button in the outline review widget, OR
  - The user explicitly asks you to generate the design after approving the outline WITHOUT requesting any changes.

WHAT YOU MUST PROVIDE:
- Use ONLY the reviewed and approved outline parameters from the widget.
- You MUST pass:
  - topic
  - audience
  - style
  - length
  - presentation_outlines (titles + descriptions exactly as approved)
- Do NOT modify, reorder, add, or remove slides unless the user has explicitly approved those changes in the outline review step.

IMPORTANT CONSTRAINTS:
- This tool must never be used as an entry point for presentation creation.
- Design generation must never bypass outline review.
- request-outline-review is the single, mandatory gateway for all presentations.

CLAUDE-SPECIFIC CONSTRAINTS:
- When calling this tool, you MUST remove all punctuation from the outline titles and descriptions before passing them in the presentation_outlines parameter
- Remove all punctuation marks (periods, commas, colons, semicolons, exclamation marks, question marks, quotes, hyphens, etc.)
- Keep only alphanumeric characters and spaces
- Normalize multiple spaces to single spaces
- Example transformation:
  - Original: "Introduction: Getting Started!"
  - Claude format: "Introduction Getting Started"
- This ensures optimal processing by the backend generation system for Claude-based requests

tools.name: read-design
tools.description:
Read a Canva design: its metadata, page content (as markdown with [locator_id] annotations), page thumbnails, and/or presenter notes — in a single call. Optionally open an editing transaction so you can immediately edit with `edit-design`.

## What you get
Use `filter.fields` to choose what to return (defaults to `design_metadata` + `design_content`):
- `design_metadata` — title, owner, URLs, page count.
- `page_metadata` — per-page metadata (index, page number, dimensions) for each page in the design. Read-only; does not require a transaction. Returns the first 50 pages unless narrowed with `filter.page_indices`.
- `design_content` — the design's text content. By default (a plain read) this is the readable text, which works with read-only access. When you open or pass an editing transaction (`open_transaction: true` or `transaction_id`), `design_content` instead becomes the full page CDF as markdown, where each element is annotated with a `[locator_id]` (e.g. `## TEXT [PBxxx-LByyy]`). Use that locator_id as the `element_id` in `edit-design` operations.
- `thumbnails` — page PNG thumbnails. Must be listed in `fields` to be returned; choose which pages with `filter.thumbnail_pages` (defaults to `filter.page_indices`, then page 1). By default these reflect the last saved version of the design. To get a thumbnail that includes uncommitted edits, pass the `transaction_id` of your open editing transaction.
- `presenter_notes` — speaker notes for presentation pages.

## Partial results
A per-field failure never fails the whole call; it is reported in a `warnings` array (`{ field, reason, code? }`) instead of being silently omitted. Check `warnings` and retry the listed field.

## Narrowing the document
- `filter.page_indices` — only return these pages (1-indexed page numbers). Also scopes `page_metadata` and `presenter_notes`.
- `filter.element_ids` — only return these elements (match by locator_id or trailing element id). Only applies when an editing transaction is in play (`open_transaction: true` or `transaction_id`); a plain read returns the full text.

## Editing
Pass `open_transaction: true` to also start an editing transaction. The response includes `transaction.transaction_id` — pass it to `edit-design` to apply operations. Opening a transaction also upgrades `design_content` to the full CDF markdown with `[locator_id]` annotations needed for editing. A plain read (no `open_transaction`) never opens a transaction, so it works for users with read-only access.
After an `edit-design` call, pass that transaction's `transaction_id` back to this tool to re-read the `design_content` and/or `thumbnails` reflecting your uncommitted edits.

design_id.description: ID of the design to read.

open_transaction.description: When true, also open an editing transaction and return its `transaction_id` for use with `edit-design`. Defaults to false.

transaction_id.description: Optional. Pass the `transaction_id` of an open editing transaction to render `design_content`/`thumbnails` from that transaction — including UNCOMMITTED edits applied via `edit-design`. Use this to re-read after editing. When omitted, the response reflects the last saved (persisted) version of the design.

element_ids.description: Only include these elements in `design_content`. Match by full locator_id (e.g. `PBxxx-LByyy`) or trailing element id (e.g. `LByyy`).

Search docs, presentations, videos, whiteboards, sheets, and other designs in Canva, except for templates or brand templates.
      Use when you need to find specific designs by keywords rather than browsing folders.
      Use 'query' parameter to search by title or content.
      If 'query' is used, 'sortBy' must be set to 'relevance'. Filter by 'any' ownership unless specified. Sort by relevance unless specified.
      Use the continuation token to get the next page of results, when there are more results.

      CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS:
      1. ALWAYS use the 'search-brand-templates' tool when the user is searching for templates or wants to use a template.
      2.** 🚫 When a user says search a template, they ALWAYS mean brand-templates. Therefore NEVER call this tool, ALWAYS call the 'search-brand-templates' tool to search for the templates. **
      3.** 🚫 NEVER use this tool when the user expresses intent to “generate”, “create”, “autofill”, “search a template”, “start from a template”, “use my template”, or “pick a template for generation”.
      In all such cases, ALWAYS use search-brand-templates.
      ANY query involving:
      – “generate a presentation”
      – “generate a report”
      – “make a design using a template”
      – “generate from a template”
      – “produce a presentation from their template”
      - "search for available templates"
      MUST NOT use search-designs.
      This tool ONLY searches existing designs (docs, presentations, whiteboards, videos, etc.) that the user already owns or that are shared with them.
      It DOES NOT find templates and MUST NOT be used as a fallback for template selection. **

tools.name: apply_script
tools.description:
Apply the edits already authored as `timeline.md` to the canonical timeline. This is the commit step for Script edits: it diffs the file against the live state and commits atomically (any single-row error rolls back the whole apply). After a successful apply, `timeline.md` is re-materialized clean (no `~~...~~`); just read it again for further edits.

# Workflow

Pair with `read_script`: first call `read_script`, then edit the materialized `timeline.md`, then call this tool.

- On surfaces with a workspace filesystem (ChatCut backend agent with a sandbox attached), edit `timeline.md` in place with `edit_workspace_file` / `write_workspace_file` (Codex plugin) or the native workspace `Edit` / `Write` tools, then call `apply_script()` with no `timelineMd`. ChatCut reads it from your workspace.
- On external surfaces without a workspace, `read_script` returned the `timelineMd` string inline; edit that string with your own tools and call `apply_script({timelineMd: "<full edited content>"})`.

For preview before commit, pass `preview: true`.

# Valid Script edits

- Remove a spoken source word from playback: `[s5] keep~~drop~~keep`
- Remove a Chinese particle with no added spaces: `[s1] 过去~~呢~~一个月`
- Remove a whole segment / clip / gap: delete the row, or write `~~[s5] text~~`
- Cut a visible silence marker: `~~[silence=0.8s]~~`
- Compress a visible silence marker: `[silence=0.8s→0.2s]`
- Reorder or replay rows by moving / duplicating them. Moving an existing `[sN@M]` row preserves that occurrence, while adding a bare `[sN]` row creates another play of that content. Author the whole arrangement (reorders, repeats, multiple versions back-to-back) and commit it in one apply.
- When duplicate timeline rows render occurrence anchors like `[s5@1]` and `[s5@2]`, preserve the `@N` suffix on the specific existing occurrence you edit, move, or delete. For hook replacement, remove only the copied hook occurrence rows, not the body occurrence.

`[sN]` rows are not freeform rewrites. They should either follow the source text or mark unwanted source text with `~~...~~`. Do not directly skip middle words (write `过去~~呢~~一个月`, not `过去一个月`), and do not invent new wording that the source never said.

Matching is tolerant to case, punctuation, and accidental word-boundary whitespace differences such as `and it` vs `andit`; it is not tolerant to changing the spoken words themselves. Use `manage_transcript` action `fix` when the transcript text is wrong.

# Expected timeline result

Applying Script edits rebuilds the timeline as clips from kept source ranges. Start/end trims can stay as a single trimmed clip. Middle deletions and middle moves cannot stay as one continuous source range: apply creates new clips for the kept ranges around the removed/moved content. More clips after this kind of edit are expected and usually correct. If visible jump cuts are distracting, cover or polish them after the A-roll edit.

# Output

The result includes a `Removed:` section listing every row that disappeared vs the previous canonical state. This is an internal post-apply audit, not user-facing language. Do not quote row ids or segment ids to the user; translate the audit into the actual spoken content or a plain-language summary.

# Caveats

- This does not correct ASR mistakes. If the source transcript text itself is wrong, use `manage_transcript` action `fix` before editing Script.
- Do not simplify an existing `[sN@M]` row to `[sN]` while editing, moving, or deleting that occurrence; that loses identity and can target the wrong duplicate. Only a newly added replay row should be bare `[sN]`.
- Each `[sN]` line must be a contiguous substring of its source segment. Do NOT rewrite or fabricate words.
- Inline strikethrough is valid: `[s4] ~~uh, ~~improvements` deletes only `uh, ` and keeps `improvements`. Never expand a user-approved inline strike to a whole-line deletion.
- If the timeline was modified externally since the last `read_script`, apply refuses (stale state). Recovery: re-materialize via `read_script`, review the new state, then re-edit and re-apply.

preview.description: Preview the result without modifying the timeline.

Do not use this for file uploads and do not add media-upload questions to the form; if a specific task needs missing source media, ask for it separately through the MCP host file-attachment flow or the ChatCut editor. For native ChatCut editor-hosted agents, keep using the native `<widget>` form protocol instead; this MCP tool is for external MCP Apps hosts.

tools.name: browse_library
tools.description:
Browse the ChatCut Library with one unified discovery tool.

This tool is for ChatCut Library content only, not the user's project assets/media pool and not timelines. Categories match the Library tabs: motion-graphics, luts, zoom, fx, audio-fx, sound-effects, transitions.

Supported modes:
- No filters: returns a whole-Library overview with category counts.
- category: returns one Library tab's group overview with counts.
- category + group: returns a small list of items in that group.
- query: returns a small matching item list, optionally scoped by category.
- id: returns one item's details plus usage guidance.
- limit + offset: paginates list results.

List results are intentionally small skill-list-style results with only id, name, category, and description. Detailed usage guidance is returned only by id mode. Execution uses edit_item for timeline placement:
- motion-graphics: call edit_item with the returned library assetId. edit_item copies the Library MG into the current project, preserves the template item's defaults, and returns the created timeline item id.
- sound-effects: call edit_item adds:[{type:"audio",assetId:"library:sound:<id>",fromFrame:<editorial moment frame>}]. edit_item imports/reuses the Library sound asset and shifts the item start so the sound anchor lands on fromFrame.
- zoom: call edit_item with the returned Library Zoom id as assetId; edit_item expands it to the built-in zoom effect and preset defaults.
- luts, fx, transitions: call edit_item with the returned usage guidance.
- audio-fx: currently has no available Library entries; an empty result is expected.

category.description: Optional Library tab/category filter: motion-graphics, luts, zoom, fx, audio-fx, sound-effects, or transitions.

group.description: Optional Library group id filter. With category, returns list results from that group.

id.description: Exact Library item id to inspect after search. Returns the chosen item plus usage guidance from this same tool.

limit.description: Maximum list results to return. Defaults to 10, max 30.

offset.description: List offset for pagination in list mode.

query.description: Case-insensitive search over id, name, category, group, description, and keywords. Supports multi-word queries and common quote/social/card/sound-effect synonyms. Passing query returns a list.

tools.name: clean_script
tools.description:
Mechanical first-pass cleanup for talking-head transcripts already on the timeline: fixed filler-token removal plus batch silence pause compression / restoration. For cleanup tasks, run this before semantic Script editing when fixed fillers or long pauses are present. Both capabilities run by default; use `only` to pick one. Runs incrementally — no-op if the bin asset isn't placed; per-item decoration and prior Script edits are preserved.

This is not a semantic speech editor. Anything that requires understanding meaning, tone, retakes, repeated ideas, or context-dependent verbal habits belongs in Script (`read_script` → `~~...~~` in `timeline.md` → `apply_script`).

# Filler-word removal

Strikes only this fixed token list:
- EN: `um / uh / er / ah`
- ZH: `呃 / 额`

Ambiguous/contextual fillers and verbal habits are excluded: `呢 / 啊 / 嗯 / mm / hmm`, repeated phrases, stutters, retakes, and semantic repetition. If the user explicitly wants one of these heard words removed, delete it with Script, e.g. `[s1] 过去~~呢~~一个月`.

# Pause / silence cleanup

Use the `silence` field to translate common pause-editing requests directly:

- Tighter breaths / compress long pauses: `silence: "compress:400"` shortens pauses longer than 400ms to 400ms.
- "Compress every pause over 0.3s to 0.3s": `silence: "compress:300"`.
- Restore more breathing room / "keep at least 0.5s": `silence: "restore:500"` makes short pauses longer, up to 500ms, only when that pause was already that long in the original recording.
- "Make pauses around 0.5s": `silence: "normalize:500"` moves every editable pause toward 500ms.
- "Keep pauses between 0.3s and 0.8s": `silence: "range:300-800"`.

Any rule that makes a pause longer — `restore`, `normalize`, or the lower bound in `range` — never invents new silence. It only recovers pause time that already existed at that exact spot in the original recording. If the original pause was shorter than the requested value, it stops at the original pause length. Legacy syntax still works: `max:400` = `compress:400`, `min:500` = `restore:500`, `500` = `normalize:500`, `min:300,max:800` = `range:300-800`.

Internally this rewrites `[silence=Xs]` → `[silence=Xs→Ys]` and applies the result to the timeline.

You do not need to expose silence markers first. `timeline.md` may hide `[silence=Ns]` by default, but clean_script materializes the needed silence information internally and applies the batch rewrite.

# When NOT to use

Do not use this for precise user-specified word deletion, `呢` / `啊` / `嗯` cleanup, choosing the best retake, deleting duplicate sentences, fixing ASR mistakes, or any edit where the right answer depends on the sentence meaning. Use Script for playback edits and `manage_transcript` action `fix` for ASR correction.

After automatic cleanup, read Script state and manually handle anything that still needs semantic judgment.

longSilence.description: Long-pause threshold in ms for the default rule (≥this → 200ms). Default 3000. Ignored when `silence` is set.

only.description: `fillers`, `silence`, or both as `fillers,silence`. Default runs both.

silence.description: Pause rule. Prefer action names: `"compress:400"` shortens pauses longer than 400ms to 400ms; `"restore:500"` makes short pauses longer up to 500ms only when that pause was already that long in the original recording; `"normalize:500"` moves every editable pause toward 500ms; `"range:300-800"` keeps pauses between 300ms and 800ms. Any rule that makes a pause longer never invents new silence; it only recovers pause time that already existed at that exact spot. Legacy syntax also works: `"max:400"`, `"min:500"`, `"500"`, `"min:300,max:800"`. To skip silence entirely, pass `only="fillers"`.

tools.name: convert_motion_graphic_to_video
tools.description:
Convert a motion graphic into a real, transparent video asset (vp8/WebM alpha).

Step 1 of the MG→video convert flow: kicks a cloud render of the MG at its native length and returns a durable renderId. Then:
  1. Call track_export with the renderId until status is "complete" and read outputUrl.
  2. Call register_converted_video with { mgAssetId, outputUrl } to import the render as a video asset in the media pool.

One MG maps to one deterministic video asset, so re-converting the same MG dedupes to the existing asset. Use this when the user wants an MG as a plain video — to overlay on footage, or to replace the MG clip with a real video clip (via edit_item after the video asset exists).

tools.name: create_motion_graphic_from_code

Use this for direct-authored Motion Graphics from inline JSX where the visual mechanism is chosen for the edit: emphasis, orientation, proof, sequence, contrast, transition, recurring identity, title/chapter beats, visual systems, exact UI callouts, debug overlays, or code-specific visualizations.

When creating MGs for multiple timeline moments, name each MG's viewer job and visual mechanism before coding. Reuse an asset only for an intentionally recurring component with the same editorial job, information structure, and visual form. Otherwise create separate assets that share palette, type, and motion logic.
If the only style input for multiple MGs is a user-named text/custom direction, create only one representative MG until the user confirms it; a text style alone is not batch permission.
After proofing a batch, compare composed settled frames side by side. Shared visual language is expected; repeated surfaces, anchors, or rhythms should point to a recurring viewer job.

Duration should match the intended timeline span, with entrance, hold, and exit motion completing inside the placed item duration.

Size: width/height are the MG's natural box around the visible local composition. For overlays, do not use a transparent timeline-sized wrapper for placement. Use timeline dimensions only for intentional full-frame MGs. Place and scale with edit_item.

This is the public-safe code path: it does not read repo files, local files, chat attachment paths, temporary HTTP servers, or backend workspace paths. The Motion Graphic code is validated by ChatCut's normal Motion Graphic validator, registered as a project asset, and appears in the media pool. This tool creates the asset only; place it on the timeline with `edit_item`. For patching an existing Motion Graphic asset, use `edit_asset` with inline `json.code`.

tools.name: edit_asset
tools.description:
Update or delete a library asset.

- update: change asset-level fields. For code-based assets (motion-graphic / effect / transition / svg), pass codeFile pointing at a workspace file, or set code:"..." inline in json. For other fields use json (e.g. filename, sourceLut). type is optional for update and inferred from assetId.
- Motion-graphic properties schema uses {key,label,type,defaultValue}. To change existing asset-level default values, use propertyDefaults:{key:value}. Clip-level MG values use edit_item propertyOverrides.
- Prefer propertyDefaults for Motion Graphic asset default values. Legacy top-level property keys such as logoImage/titleText/fontFamily are normalized to propertyDefaults only when type:"motion-graphic" is explicit; height/width remain clip/source dimensions, and duration is normalized to durationInSeconds.
- Source LUT on original media: set sourceLut:null on video/image/gif to remove, or sourceLut:{assetId,name?} to apply.
- delete: remove the asset and any items/effects/transitions that reference it. If references exist, the tool first returns the impact and requires confirmImpact:true before deleting.

Asset properties live on the asset; clip-level position and per-instance overrides live on the item — use edit_item for those.

External MCP asset-code rule: workspace files are not available on this connector. To update code-based assets, first read the current code with inspect_asset({ assetId, code: true }), then pass the full replacement source inline as json.code, for example json: {"type":"motion-graphic","code":"..."}. Do not use codeFile.

tools.name: edit_captions
tools.description:
Manage captions/subtitles. To inspect caption text content, use the read-only `read_captions` tool.

# When to read first
- `display_text` (hide / mask / split / merge / re-text SPECIFIC words) is the ONLY action that needs a read: call `read_captions {"words":true}` for the word `key`s, then put every word in ONE `display_text` call.
- To inspect built-in presets for the current caption languages, call `template` with no preset; it resolves the language-aware catalog without a separate `read_captions` call.
- Every other action is a single direct call — no read first, and never re-read only to verify (the result lists what it changed).

# Actions

## Lifecycle
- `enable` / `disable` — toggle captions. First-pass/default source behavior is `sourceScope:{mode:"timeline"}`: captions read every audible timeline source, not a single V1/A1 track. For captions with no aesthetic request, omit `preset`; omitted `preset` and `preset:"auto"` both mean the default Plain visual style with Auto segmentation. For a generic aesthetic request, enable first and then use the language-aware `template` catalog. `enable` also accepts a built-in preset name via the `preset` field when the user explicitly asks for that specific look. Do NOT pass `trackId` / `trackOrder` to `enable`; to narrow to a specific source after enabling, use `source_set`.

## Display override
- `display_text` — change what the caption SHOWS without rewriting the transcript (profanity mask, filler hide, punctuation tweaks, small display-only wording). For translated/bilingual subtitles, first use `language_mode` so the translation source exists; then `read_captions {"words":true}` exposes translation word keys and `display_text` may edit those translated words. Do NOT create an entire translation by writing original-language words into display overrides — use `language_mode` / `manage_transcript` translation instead. For correcting the underlying source transcript itself, use `manage_transcript` action `fix`. To reset display-only edits, pass `{"clearOverrides":true}` (alias `clear_overrides`) to clear all word display overrides for this captions item, or per word pass `text:null`, `hidden:false`, `forcePageBreak:false`, / `keepWithPrevious:false`. Per-word layout flags ride on the same override: `hidden:true` hides a word; `forcePageBreak:true` breaks the page immediately BEFORE that word — the word becomes the FIRST word of a new caption card (the break is before it, not after; to keep a word on the current card, set the break on the word that should START the next card). It lets you split a line into separate sequential cards at an exact point the global wordsPerPage/maxCharactersPerLine won't pick (e.g. set it on the words "我"/"yt" so "你好,我是yt,很高兴认识你" shows as 你好 / 我是 / yt很高兴认识你). Pass `forcePageBreak:false` to clear a break. It subdivides only — a forced segment still wraps per maxLines if long. `keepWithPrevious:true` is the INVERSE — it MERGES this word's card into the previous one (never breaks before it) even where the engine would split for width/clause; the merged card keeps the configured font size and may need higher `maxLines` / `maxCharactersPerLine` if it is too dense. Use it to glue a deliberate clause break — set it on the FIRST word of the card you want pulled up. Pass `keepWithPrevious:false` to clear. (keep wins if both keepWithPrevious and forcePageBreak are set on one word.) IMPORTANT: if a card split because the SENTENCE is too long, do NOT hand-merge each fragment — RAISE `maxLines` / `maxCharactersPerLine` in one `style` call (no read needed; `read_captions` shows `break=length` if you want to confirm).

## Style
A caption's look can be changed with a built-in preset (`template`) or explicit custom fields (`style`). Prefer built-in presets because they provide more stable results.
- `template` — list or apply built-in caption presets. Call `template` with no `templatePreset`/`preset` to read the language-aware catalog. It returns entries with `id`, English `name`, Chinese-catalog `localizedName`, `styleProfile` (actual visual behavior, excluding font size/position), and `paginationProfile` (creation defaults). Chinese, including bilingual captions with Chinese, gets the curated Chinese preset catalog. Apply a returned preset by passing `templatePreset` (preferred) or the legacy `preset` alias. Applying a template to existing captions preserves their current size, position, and pagination. A valid built-in may also be applied directly by name. This is separate from USER-saved `preset_*` actions.
- `style` — set explicit custom fields (see "# Style fields" below). Fields left unset are inherited from the current caption. For current-word highlight: set `highlightColor`, `highlightBackground`, or `highlightUnit` only when that behavior should change; otherwise omit them so the current preset/item behavior is preserved. To remove highlight, pass `highlightOff: true`. Box geometry — `width` / `left` / `top` / size / position — is NOT a style field; set it with action=`layout` (e.g. a word pushed onto the next line because the box is too narrow → widen via `layout`, not `style`).
- Whichever route is used, every attribute the user explicitly stated (a color, a band, a highlight, a case) must end up applied; layer `style` on top of `template` when explicit requested details are not part of the preset.
- `preset_save` / `preset_apply` / `preset_rename` / `preset_delete` / `preset_list` — manage USER-saved style presets (separate from built-in `template`).

## Layout
- `layout` — position the WHOLE caption block. Exact pixels (`left` / `top` / `right` / `bottom` / `width` / `height`) or preset (`bottom` / `top` / `center`, or 3×3 title-safe: `top-left` / `top-center` / `top-right` / `middle-left` / `middle-center` / `middle-right` / `bottom-left` / `bottom-center` / `bottom-right`). For placing each language/source separately (e.g. English on top, Chinese at the bottom) use `positions`, not `layout` — `layout` moves both lines together.

## Source
- `track` — legacy/debug only: change the captions item's storage/legacy source `trackId`. Captions render as one timeline-level overlay; `trackId` only anchors the captions item to a timeline and remains the legacy single-source fallback when no `sourceScope` is set. Do NOT use `track` to choose the visible caption text source; use `source_set` instead.

## Multi-source (one captions item, several speakers/languages on screen)
- `language_mode` — canonical user-facing language switch for captions. Use this for "add bilingual captions", "show only English", "restore original captions", or "translate captions to X". Pass `{"mode":"original"}`, `{"mode":"translation","languageCode":"en"}`, or `{"mode":"bilingual","languageCode":"en","primary":"original"}`. IMPORTANT: `languageCode` is the TRANSLATION TARGET language, not the source/original language and not the name of a bilingual pair. For "Chinese + English / 中英字幕", first infer or read the current original language, then choose the OTHER language as `languageCode`: if the original speech is English and the user wants Chinese above English, call `{"mode":"bilingual","languageCode":"zh","primary":"translation"}`; if the original speech is Chinese and the user wants Chinese above English, call `{"mode":"bilingual","languageCode":"en","primary":"original"}`. Never translate to the same language as the original just because the user named that language in the pair; that creates English+English or Chinese+Chinese. `primary:"translation"` puts the translated line on top. For translation/bilingual modes, this action first ensures the translation variant exists (incremental, reuses fresh rows), then writes the caption sourceScope. Optional `regenerate:true` forces a fresh translation. Optional scope fields `trackId` / `itemId` / `assetId` / `allSpoken:true` narrow the translation; default is `allSpoken:true` for the active timeline. Use this instead of manually chaining `manage_transcript translation_ensure` + `source_set` for ordinary language requests.
- `bilingual` — one-shot upgrade of the current captions to bilingual: keeps the existing original source and adds a translation layer reading the SAME speech, then auto-stacks them. Pass ONLY a translation target language object such as `{"languageCode":"en"}`; do not pass a `sources` array to this action. `languageCode` has the same rule as `language_mode`: it is the language to TRANSLATE INTO, so do not pass the original language. Optional `primary`: `"original"` (default) puts the source language on top with the translation below; `"translation"` flips it so the viewer-language translation is on top (going-overseas case). Sources stack first-on-top, so primary just sets their order. PRECONDITION: the translation must already exist — run `manage_transcript` action `translation_ensure` for that language first, or this resolves to an empty translation layer. The translation line shows the whole sentence with no per-word highlight (translation word timings are interpolated; karaoke follows variant, not stack position, so flipping `primary` never changes highlighting). Idempotent: re-running with the same language + primary never duplicates the translation layer; re-running with a different `primary` just reorders the existing pair. Use this instead of hand-assembling two sources via `source_set` for the common "show the original plus one translation" case; reach for `source_set` only when you need finer control (specific tracks/speakers, styling, or more than two languages).
- `source_list` — show the current source scope, layout policy, visual source order, and available tracks.
- `source_set` — replace the whole source scope on the same captions item. For normal "caption every audible speaking track on this timeline", pass `{"mode":"timeline"}`. For explicit sources, pass `sources` (array). Each source is `{trackId|assetId|itemId|speakerId, variant?, variantKind?, languageCode?, label?, priority?, slotId?}`. `variant` selects which transcript to show: `{"variantKind":"translation","languageCode":"en"}` for a translation. Create it first with `manage_transcript` action `translation_ensure`, then use the returned `applyToCaptionSource` action/json. Omit variant fields for the original. In auto-stack, sources render top-to-bottom in the order listed — the FIRST source is on top — so list the original first for original-on-top, or list the translation first to put it on top. In single-lane, the same order is priority when sources overlap. Pass `{"sourceScope":null}` to clear and go back to the single-track source.
- `source_add` — append one source (`{"source":{...}}`) to the existing scope.
- `source_remove` — remove a source by passing the selector at the TOP LEVEL: `{"index":1}`, `{"trackId":"V1"}`, `{"assetId":"..."}`, `{"itemId":"..."}`, `{"slotId":"..."}`, `{"speakerId":"..."}`, `{"id":"..."}`, or `{"sourceId":"..."}`. Removing the last source reverts to the legacy single-track source.
- `source_update` — update one or more logical caption sources without moving caption tracks/items. Use this for source-specific presentation: `{"updates":[{"trackId":"V2","anchor":"bottom-center","offsetYRatio":-0.08,"visible":true,"style":{"sizePx":72,"highlightBackground":{"color":"#facc15","paddingX":18,"paddingY":8,"borderRadius":10}}},{"trackId":"V1","anchor":"top-center","offsetYRatio":0.08,"style":{"sizePx":48}}]}`. A source update can select by `index`, `sourceId` / `id`, `trackId`, `assetId`, `itemId`, `speakerId`, `label`, or nested `variant`; it can set `visible`, `anchor`, `slotId`, `preset`, `style`, `variant`, and slot geometry `widthRatio` / `heightRatio` / `offsetXRatio` / `offsetYRatio`. To switch a source to English, either pass `variant:{"variantKind":"translation","languageCode":"en"}` or the shorthand `variantKind:"translation", languageCode:"en"` on that source update.
- `layout_policy` — how multiple sources share the screen. `{"mode":"single-lane"}` makes sources share the SAME caption position (best for VO and camera/audio tracks that alternate over time; if two sources overlap, priority/maxVisibleSources decides which is shown). `{"mode":"auto-stack","maxVisibleSources":2}` keeps sources in separate stacked bands (best for bilingual/simultaneous speech). `{"mode":"manual-slots","slots":[{"id":"top","anchor":"top-center","offsetYRatio":0.08},{"id":"bottom","anchor":"bottom-center","offsetYRatio":-0.08}]}` pins sources to explicit positions. Slot geometry uses ratios: `widthRatio`, `heightRatio`, `offsetXRatio`, `offsetYRatio`. Per-source overrides go in `perSource` keyed by `sourceId` (from `source_list`): `{"perSource":{"<sourceId>":{"maxLines":2}}}` lets one stream wrap to more lines than the shared item `maxLines` (e.g. original 1 line, translation 2) — by default both stacked lines share the item `maxLines`. Pass `{"layoutPolicy":null}` to clear.
- `positions` — place multiple sources in one call. Different anchors build manual slots (for example English top-center and Chinese bottom-center). If multiple sources use the same anchor, ChatCut treats them as one normal stacked subtitle block at that anchor, not overlapping manual boxes. `{"positions":[{"index":0,"anchor":"bottom-center","offsetYRatio":-0.08},{"index":1,"anchor":"top-center","offsetYRatio":0.08}]}`. Identify each source by `index`, `variant` (e.g. `{"variantKind":"translation","languageCode":"en"}`), `label`, `trackId`, `assetId`, `itemId`, `speakerId`, `id`, or `sourceId` — `index` / `variant` are easiest when two languages share one track. `anchor` is the 3×3 set (`top-center`, `bottom-center`, ...). Per-source placement uses ratios; pixel `left` / `top` / `width` / `height` belongs to whole-block `layout`, not `positions` or `source_update`.

To show a translation: prefer `language_mode` because it ensures the translation and switches the caption source in one call. Use `manage_transcript` action `translation_ensure` + returned `applyToCaptionSource` only for advanced/debug workflows. Do not create another captions item or video track just to separate caption languages/styles.

# Style fields

For the `style` action, pass any combination via `json`:

- **text** — `font`, `sizePx` (preferred human unit) or `fontSizeRatio` (stored internally as `sizePx / min(canvasWidth, canvasHeight)`, 0–1), `color`, `opacity` (0–1), `weight`, `variant`, `align`
- **stroke** — `strokeColor`, `strokeWidth`, `strokeOpacity`, `strokeOff`
- **current-word highlight** — `highlightColor` = active-word TEXT color. `highlightBackground` = a pill behind the active word, an object `{color, paddingX, paddingY, borderRadius, animation}` where `animation` is `"none"` (default) / `"fade"` / `"slide"` / `"bounce"`; it MERGES by key, so pass only what changes (e.g. `{"animation":"bounce"}` keeps the existing color). `highlightUnit` = `"word"` (karaoke that follows speech) / `"line"` (whole line lit at once) / `"off"` (none). For a plain "highlight the current word in <color>" request set `highlightColor` only; add `highlightBackground` only when the user wants a pill. Setting either `highlightColor` or `highlightBackground` auto-turns the highlight on (incl. CJK, off by default) — you needn't also pass `highlightUnit`. Turn highlight off with `highlightUnit:"off"`. (Unset default: CJK = off; every other language = `"word"`.)
- **background** — band behind the whole line: `backgroundColor`, `backgroundOpacity` (0–1), `backgroundRadius`; `backgroundOff:true` clears
- **shadow** — `shadowStrength` (0–100) or raw CSS `shadow` (e.g. `"0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,.85)"`); `shadowOff:true` clears
- **typography** — `maxLines` (lines per card) + `maxCharactersPerLine` (per-line character cap before wrapping; alias `maxCharsPerLine`. Counts characters, so a CJK glyph counts as 1 even though it renders ~2× wider than a Latin letter — use a smaller cap for CJK, ~half the Latin value). These two SET THE PER-CARD CAPACITY: a sentence that doesn't fit (maxLines × maxCharsPerLine) splits into another card (read_captions marks it `break=length`). So to KEEP WHOLE SENTENCES on one card / stop length-splitting, RAISE `maxLines` (and/or `maxCharsPerLine`) in this ONE call — don't hand-merge each fragment with keepWithPrevious. Also: `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`, `textTransform` (`"none"` / `"uppercase"`, the panel's Aa/AA case control), `direction`
- **pacing (display granularity)** — for ANY "automatic/natural / a few words / one word at a time" request, set `pacing`: `"auto"` (natural sentence/clause/pause paging; this is the canonical name), `"phrase"` (a few words), or `"word"` (one word per card — TikTok). `"sentence"` is accepted only as a legacy alias for `"auto"`; it is NOT a stricter "never split a sentence" mode. ALWAYS apply `pacing` when the user asks for one of these — in ONE `style` call, without reading first; don't skip because the current pagination already looks close (the user asked to set it, so set it). Pacing controls DENSITY only: it sets `wordsPerPage` and never touches `maxLines` (the height axis stays whatever the user has). Do NOT hand-pick a `wordsPerPage` number to approximate them; use raw `wordsPerPage` (`1`–`12`) ONLY for a deliberate exact per-card word cap that isn't one of the named modes; `wordsPerPage:null` = natural paging. A "TikTok-style word-by-word" request is just `pacing:"word"`; reach for the `tiktok` template only when the user wants the full TikTok visual aesthetic (font/color/highlight), then layer `pacing:"word"` on top.
- **display** — `displayMode` (`"single"` = one card / `"stacked"` = paper-card stack of recent lines), `hidePunctuation` (`true` hides punctuation at render only; timing/transcript untouched), `textTransform` (`"none"` for Aa / `"uppercase"` for AA)

# Examples

- Enable with the Plain default and all audible timeline sources: `{"action":"enable"}`
- Narrow captions to a specific voiceover track after enabling: `{"action":"source_set","json":"{\"sources\":[{\"trackId\":\"A1\"}]}"}`
- List built-in caption presets with style and pagination profiles: `{"action":"template"}`
- Apply a built-in caption preset: `{"action":"template","templatePreset":"deyi-card"}`
- Custom style: `{"action":"style","json":"{\"sizePx\":72,\"color\":\"#FFF\",\"shadowStrength\":45}"}`
- Profanity mask (get `key` from `read_captions`): `{"action":"display_text","json":"{\"overrides\":[{\"key\":\"abc123:def456\",\"text\":\"****\"}]}"}`
- Bulk hide selected words: `{"action":"display_text","json":"{\"selectedWordEntryIds\":[\"a:b\",\"c:d\"],\"hidden\":true}"}`
- Clear all display-only word overrides on this captions item: `{"action":"display_text","json":"{\"clearOverrides\":true}"}`
- Force page breaks (new card starts at each listed word): `{"action":"display_text","json":"{\"overrides\":[{\"key\":\"a:b\",\"forcePageBreak\":true},{\"key\":\"c:d\",\"forcePageBreak\":true}]}"}`
- Merge a card into the previous one (set on its FIRST word; no need to touch box width): `{"action":"display_text","json":"{\"overrides\":[{\"key\":\"a:b\",\"keepWithPrevious\":true}]}"}`
- Caption all audible timeline sources: `{"action":"source_set","json":"{\"mode\":\"timeline\"}"}`
- Put alternating VO/video-source captions in the same on-screen position: `{"action":"layout_policy","json":"{\"mode\":\"single-lane\"}"}`
- Add Chinese+English captions when original speech is English, Chinese on top: `{"action":"language_mode","json":"{\"mode\":\"bilingual\",\"languageCode\":\"zh\",\"primary\":\"translation\"}"}`
- Add Chinese+English captions when original speech is Chinese, Chinese on top: `{"action":"language_mode","json":"{\"mode\":\"bilingual\",\"languageCode\":\"en\",\"primary\":\"original\"}"}`
- Show only the English translation: `{"action":"language_mode","json":"{\"mode\":\"translation\",\"languageCode\":\"en\"}"}`
- Restore original-language captions: `{"action":"language_mode","json":"{\"mode\":\"original\"}"}`
- Common bilingual original + English after the English translation exists: `{"action":"bilingual","json":"{\"languageCode\":\"en\"}"}`
- Custom bilingual/source arrangement: `{"action":"source_set","json":"{\"sources\":[{\"trackId\":\"V1\"},{\"trackId\":\"V1\",\"variantKind\":\"translation\",\"languageCode\":\"en\"}]}"}`
- Remove the second source: `{"action":"source_remove","json":"{\"index\":1}"}`
- Rename a saved preset: `{"action":"preset_rename","json":"{\"name\":\"Podcast punch\",\"newName\":\"Podcast clean\"}"}`
- Title-safe layout: `{"action":"layout","json":"{\"preset\":\"bottom-center\"}"}`

tools.description:
Item-level timeline operations across types: `video` (incl. B-roll cutaways), `audio`, `image`, `gif`, `svg`, `motion-graphic`, `effect`, `transition`. Existing legacy `solid` items may be deleted, but edit_item does not create, duplicate, or update solids; use opaque Motion Graphics for title cards, backgrounds, and color mattes. # Safety defaults

- `validateOnly:true`: dry-run validation/planning; no commit; preview IDs are not reusable. Do not combine with `ripple:true`.
- Preserve existing timeline item positions by default. Use `ripple:true` when the edit intent clearly implies inserting into an existing sequence, making room, shifting later items, or closing gaps.
- "Add/place/move to 5s" is not by itself a ripple request. If no exact track is required, omit `trackId` so auto-placement can choose a non-overlapping track; updates first try the original track, then may move only that updated item to avoid overlap.
- If the user names an exact track and the range overlaps, do not silently move other items; ask or use `validateOnly:true` to compare new layer vs replacement vs ripple insertion.

## adds — create items

- Required: media-backed items need `type` + `assetId`; `fromItemId` duplicates an existing committed item. Do not create or duplicate `solid` items; create an opaque Motion Graphic for cards, backgrounds, and color fills.
- Library Motion Graphics from `browse_library` can be added the same way as project assets: `{type:"motion-graphic",assetId:"library:motion-graphic:<id>"}`. edit_item copies the Library MG into the project and preserves its default size/duration/propertyOverrides.
- Library Sound Effects from `browse_library` use `{type:"audio",assetId:"library:sound:<id>",fromFrame:<anchor frame>}`. For these adds only, `fromFrame` is the sound's anchor/editorial moment frame; edit_item imports/reuses the project audio asset, keeps the full audio, and shifts the actual item start so the anchor lands there.
- Library Zoom presets from `browse_library` can be added as effects with `assetId:"library:zoom:<preset>"`. edit_item expands the preset to `builtin:zoom` and applies its default shape/magnification.
- Full-screen opaque Motion Graphics own their background. Do not add a separate `solid` underneath one just to set card color; set the MG `bgColor` / `transparentBackground` properties instead.
- Asset type must match item type: audio items require audio assets. A video asset with embedded audio is still `type:"video"`; add it as video to keep embedded audio, or extract/upload a separate audio asset for independent audio-only placement.
- Position: `fromFrame` for exact frames; `from` for explicit time strings; `alignTo:"track-end"|"timeline-end"`; or `trackId` only to append on that track.
- Duration: required for `image` / `gif` / `svg`; `video` / `audio` / `motion-graphic` infer asset duration when omitted. Use `durationInFrames` for exact edits.
- Source offsets: use `sourceStartFromInSeconds` for video / audio / gif source trimming; source range must stay inside the asset. Video keeps visual + embedded audio timing together.
- Layout: visual adds may use `opacity`, `width`/`height`, anchors, `rotation`, `fit`, `crop*`, `borderRadius`, and fade fields. `fit:"cover"` / `fit:"contain"` can target the whole canvas or a manual box (`left`/`top`/`width`/`height`, or right/bottom anchors); do not combine `fit` with explicit `crop*`.
- Stacking: V1 = back. Omit `trackId` for non-overlap auto-placement; this avoids same-track time overlap, not canvas overlap.
- **`fromItemId` must reference an already-committed item** — to duplicate a freshly-added item, use a second `edit_item` call after `read_project`.

## updates — modify items

`{id, ...changedFields}` (id can be a 6-char prefix from `read_project`). Editable fields by category:

- Timeline guard: pass `timelineId` from `manage_timelines list` when intentionally updating an item on a specific timeline. Without it, stale item IDs from inactive timelines are rejected.
- Position: `fromFrame` / `fromDeltaFrames` / `trackId`. Omit `trackId` to preserve the current track when possible, or auto-move only this item to a non-overlapping track when the new time would collide. Pass `trackId` to require an exact track; exact-track overlap still errors.
- Timing/source: `durationInFrames`; `playbackRate` only for `audio` / `gif` / `video`; use `sourceStartFromInSeconds` to trim the start of video/audio/gif source media.
- Audio: prefer `decibelAdjustment` for exact dB changes; `0` means unchanged, `-60` is effectively silent. Compatibility aliases `volume` / `audioVolume` accept only 0–1 linear slider values (`0` silent, `1` unchanged) and `muted:true` means silent; do not pass values above 1 to those aliases. Use `audioFadeIn`, `audioFadeOut` for fades. For "duck music under voice/speech", use `edit_track` roles instead: voice/speech track `role:"anchor"`, BGM/background music track `role:"follower"`; leave `audioRouting.duckDepthDb` unset unless the user explicitly asks for more or less music under speech.
- Visual: `opacity`, size/anchors, `rotation`, `fit`, `crop*`, `borderRadius`, `fadeIn`, `fadeOut`.
- Aspect-locked: for raw manual resize, pass only one of `width`/`height`. Use `fit:"cover"` / `fit:"contain"` when you want the tool to preserve aspect ratio automatically, including fitting into a manual box; do not combine `fit` with explicit `crop*`.

**Immutable**: `type`, `assetId`, `fromItemId`. To swap an asset → `deletes` + `adds` in the same call. Delete+add does not automatically copy the old item's source/layout fields — read the old item and include the `fromFrame`, `durationInFrames`, `trackId`, `sourceStartFromInSeconds`, crop/layout/fades/etc. you want to preserve.

**MG `propertyOverrides`**: PATCH semantics — merges with existing. `null` per-key removes override; `propertyOverrides: null` clears all. Discover valid property keys/types with `read_project` item/asset detail before guessing. For MG code itself, use `edit_asset`. **Caveat**: shrinking a motion-graphic outer item's `duration` truncates the baked inner animation — regenerate the MG asset for a different duration instead.

# Fades

Use native fade fields for ordinary fade-in/fade-out requests. Fade values are seconds, not frames:

- Visual opacity fades: `fadeIn`, `fadeOut`.
- Audio/video volume fades: `audioFadeIn`, `audioFadeOut`. On audio-only items, `fadeIn` / `fadeOut` are accepted as audio fades.
- Example: `audioFadeOut:1.5` means a 1.5-second audio fade-out. At 30fps, a 60-frame fade is `audioFadeOut:2` or `audioFadeOutDurationInFrames:60`; do not write `audioFadeOut:60` unless you want 60 seconds.
- Add separate media or Motion Graphic overlay/matte items only when the user explicitly asks for an independent visual layer.

## deletes — remove items

`{id}` or `{id, type}` (`type` required for `effect` / `transition`). Pass `timelineId` when deleting an item on a specific or non-active timeline.

## Multi-timeline targeting

Edits target the active timeline by default. To intentionally edit a different timeline without switching, pass that timeline's prefix/full id from `manage_timelines list` as `timelineId` on each `adds[]`, `updates[]`, or `deletes[]` entry. Track aliases like `V1` / `A1` then resolve inside that target timeline. If the item ID and `timelineId` disagree, the tool rejects the edit instead of silently mutating the wrong cut.

# When NOT to use — transcript-based editing → Script

If the requested end state changes which spoken words, sentences, transcript segments, topics, highlights, or takes play, use Script (`read_script` → `Edit timeline.md` → `apply_script`), not `edit_item`. `sourceStartFromInSeconds` is media addressing, not transcript-based speech selection.

# Captions boundary

Do not use `edit_item` for captions. Captions are not normal timeline items and should not be moved, trimmed, deleted, or counted through timeline-track item operations. Use `edit_captions` and `read_captions`.

# Canvas placement (adds and updates)

For background/full-bleed visuals, prefer `fit:"cover"` with no manual geometry. For a crop-to-box or contain-in-box placement, combine `fit` with a target rectangle, for example `{fit:"cover", left:50, top:880, width:160, height:160}`. Without `fit`, manual placement passes dimensions plus one horizontal anchor (`left` or `right`) and one vertical anchor (`top` or `bottom`); do not pass both sides on an axis.

# Effects, transitions

- **Effect on a clip**: `{type:"effect", targetItemId, assetId}`. `targetItemId` is the existing video/image/gif item to receive the effect; do not use `fromItemId` for effects (that field duplicates regular media items). This lands exactly like dragging the effect from the library onto the clip: a track FX in the clip's FX lane, covering the clip's full range and following the clip when it moves. Effects do not apply to motion-graphic items.
- **Effect on a track range**: `{type:"effect", assetId:"builtin:zoom", trackId:"V1", fromFrame:120, durationInFrames:60}` or the explicit `trackBoundFrom` / `trackBoundDurationInFrames` fields. Anchors to the clip under the range start; over empty track space it becomes an adjustment-layer FX spanning the range.
- **Layout is a track FX, not manual geometry**: add built-in layout assets with the same effect shape. Use `targetItemId` for a clip-scoped layout that affects only that clip; use an existing `trackId` + range on an empty/top FX lane for an adjustment-layout that dynamically wraps eligible visible video/image/gif clips below it. Built-ins: `builtin:layout-screen-face-bubble`, `builtin:layout-social-screen-stack`, `builtin:layout-two-up-split`.
- **Layout examples**: clip PiP frame treatment → `{type:"effect", assetId:"builtin:layout-screen-face-bubble", targetItemId:"cameraClipId"}`; dynamic auto split screen over sources below an existing host lane → `{type:"effect", assetId:"builtin:layout-two-up-split", trackId:"V3", fromFrame:0, durationInFrames:180}`. Do not resize clips by hand unless the user asks to bake/detach a layout.
- **Layout tuning**: after reading the `fx-track:<id>` from `read_project`, update the effect id with `propertyOverrides:{__chatcutLayout:{...}}`. The layout payload is PATCH-like for the versioned layout config: `params` patches high-leverage controls such as `bubblePosition`, `bubbleSizeRatio`, `bubbleRadiusRatio`, `gapRatio`, `paddingRatio`, `safeMarginRatio`, `fit`, and `focalIntent`; `captionPlacement` changes the layout caption policy; `sourcePolicy.pinnedRoles` pins roles such as `screen`, `camera`, `primary`, and `secondary` to item ids. For panel layouts (`layout-two-up-split` and `layout-social-screen-stack`), `params.fit` controls scaling: `cover` = Scale full frame with crop/default, `contain` = Scale entire image to fit, `fit-width` = Fit width; do not use `fill` unless the user explicitly asks to stretch/distort media.
- **Screen + Face Bubble margin**: this preset intentionally defaults to a small safe margin. Do not set `paddingRatio:0` or `safeMarginRatio:0` unless the user asks for edge-to-edge bubble placement.
- **Face-tracked zoom**: for real-time face tracking, first add or find a `builtin:zoom` track FX, then call `apply_zoom_tracking` on its `fx-track:<prefix>` id. Do not fake tracking by setting `focalMode:"track"` without a real `__chatcutReframeCurve`.
- **AI reframe curve foundation**: use `assetId:"builtin:zoom"` with reserved `propertyOverrides.__chatcutReframeCurve` only when you have a versioned `ReframeCurveV1` payload (`version:1`, `timebase:"effect-frame"`, `coordinateSpace:"composition-normalized"`, sparse keyframes with `frame`, `focalPointX`, `focalPointY`, `magnification`). Do not mutate `crop*` every few frames or invent another curve shape. `magnification` accepts 0.05-16; values below 1 zoom out, ordinary UI zooms usually stay 1-4, and explicit close-up requests like 8x are allowed.
- Either way the effect IS a track FX — there is no separate per-clip effect kind. `read_project` lists it under the track's `track-fx`; update/delete uses that id with `type:"effect"`.
- **LUT** (effect with `category="lut"`): same shape, `propertyOverrides: {intensity: 0–1}`. Swap → delete + add with a different `assetId`.
- **Add/replace transition**: `{type:"transition", assetId, outgoingItemId, incomingItemId}`; boundary shorthand `{type:"transition", assetId, trackId:"V1", fromFrame:120, durationInFrames:30}` works only when endpoints are unambiguous. Built-in transition assets use `builtin:tr-*` ids (e.g. `builtin:tr-cross-dissolve`, `builtin:tr-dip-to-black`, audio cross fade `builtin:tr-audio-cross-fade`); pass one as `assetId`. If the seam already has a transition of the same kind (visual vs audio), this replaces/updates that transition instead of duplicating it; existing duration is preserved unless `durationInFrames` is explicitly passed. Pass `replaceExisting:false` only when you want duplicate detection to error.
- **`targetItemId` / `outgoingItemId` / `incomingItemId` must reference existing items**. To add a new item AND attach an effect/transition to it, use two calls (add the item, `read_project` for the new id, then add the effect/transition).

# Ripple

`ripple:true` is timeline-movement mode: adds push later items forward; deletes close gaps. Use it when the requested edit is naturally an insertion, gap close, or sequence rewrite; do not use it merely because an overlap happened.

# Examples

- **Dry-run**: pass `validateOnly:true` with the same `adds` / `updates` / `deletes` you plan to commit.
- **Swap B-roll**: `deletes:[{id:"old"}]`, `adds:[{type:"video",assetId:"new",fromFrame:120,durationInFrames:60,trackId:"V1"}]`
- **Add 30s at timeline 5s without moving existing items**: `adds:[{type:"video",assetId:"...",from:"5s",duration:"30s"}]` (omit `trackId` so auto-placement can choose a non-overlapping track)
- **Splice 4 videos on V1**: `adds:[{...,"alignTo":"track-end"}, {...,"alignTo":"track-end"}, ...]` (chained)
- **Rebuild a track**: list every existing item id in `deletes` and the new layout in `adds` — atomic, no overlap.

tools.name: edit_track
tools.description:
Manage tracks. Actions: list | create | update | delete | tighten.

Track effects (auto-ducking, etc.) come from per-track roles, so aim for ONE role per track: before tagging roles, use the track that actually contains the relevant clips. Talking-head speech often lives on the main video track's embedded audio (for example V1), not on A1. Put music below the speech-bearing track when possible; short track names help.

- list: return the current track order with stable ids and aliases. Read-only; prefer this when you need to discover the latest aliases before another edit.
- create: create one or more tracks. JSON: {"trackType":"video"} or {"trackType":"video","count":4} (order defaults after existing tracks, which is visually on top for video). Pass "order":N as a zero-based list position; for video tracks, lower order / V1 is behind, higher order / larger V alias renders on top. Audio is inverted: A1 (lowest order) is the top lane, and higher order sits below. The result includes stable track ids; use those ids for follow-up item/caption edits because aliases like V1/V2 can shift when inserting tracks. Optionally set "role":"anchor" (a voice/speech track whose item ranges trigger ducking) or "role":"follower" (BGM/background music tracks that duck under anchors); omit for a track outside ducking. A follower's volume is automatically lowered where its items overlap anchor item ranges. Optional "name" labels the track. Optional "audioRouting.duckDepthDb" manually tunes the duck when the user asks for more/less music under speech; otherwise leave it unset so the tool can auto-initialize a depth from timeline loudness when available.
- update: change order, hidden, muted, role, name, or audioRouting. For order, pass a zero-based list position; for video overlays, use the highest-order video track / largest V alias to render above existing video. Setting "role":"follower" lowers that track's volume wherever its items overlap anchor items and reinitializes duck depth unless you pass an explicit audioRouting.duckDepthDb. Setting "role":"anchor" marks a voice track whose items trigger ducking; set "role":null to turn ducking off for that track. For speech clarity, use anchor/follower roles instead of item-level music gain changes. Do not pass audioRouting.duckDepthDb unless the user explicitly wants the ducked music louder or softer; pass audioRouting.duckDepthDb:null to clear a manual value and let the tool derive the depth again. The result includes the resulting track order with stable ids and aliases.
- delete: remove an empty track only — it is refused while clips, track FX, layouts, zooms, or adjustment clips still live on that track. For several empty tracks, use ONE call via trackIds (never one call per track). All refs are resolved and preflighted against the current state before anything is deleted, so passing V2 and V3 together is safe even though aliases renumber after each removal. A batch must stay on one timeline. The result includes the remaining track order with stable ids and aliases.
- tighten: close gaps between items on the track by snapping each item to the end of the previous one.

tools.name: find_transcript
tools.description:
Find the **timestamp** of a spoken phrase — a time-coordinate lookup, not a transcript reader or editing tool.

# What this tool is for

Locating WHEN something is said, so you can anchor non-transcript objects (B-roll, motion graphics, markers, brand overlays) at that moment. Returns:
- **Source** timestamp (`MM:SS.mmm`) — position inside the asset's media
- **Timeline placements** — every item on the timeline that plays the matched source range, with track alias + item id + frame range (`Nf`). Multi-track / multi-copy aware.

# Scope filters (all optional)

| Filter | Behavior | Search corpus |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _none_ | Search every transcribed asset used on the active timeline. | **Timeline-played** words only — what the viewer actually hears. Edits (deleted fillers, cut takes) are respected. |
| `asset` | Search one asset's raw transcript regardless of timeline use. | **Raw asset transcript** — every word from the source, ignoring edits. Use for library lookups. |
| `track` | Restrict to assets used on that track. | Timeline-played (same as _none_, narrowed to the track). |
| `asset` + `track` | Intersection — raw asset transcript filtered to that asset's instances on that track. | Raw asset transcript. |

# Matching

- Default = case + Unicode-punctuation + whitespace insensitive **contiguous** match. "DaVinci Resolve" matches "davinci resolve", "DaVinci, resolve", "DaVinci—Resolve".
- `fuzzy: true` = token-order match with window tolerance. Use when ASR may have fillers ("uh,") between query tokens.
- Word-level precision on the returned start / end timestamps.
- **Timeline-mode** (no `asset` filter): a phrase can span ASR segment boundaries and can span multiple items on the same track (e.g. two takes stitched together after editing out a filler in the middle). Phrases that were edited out won't match. Timeline placements may list multiple segments — one per item the phrase crosses.
- **Asset-mode** (with `asset` filter): contiguous-within-ASR-segment match only — a phrase crossing an ASR segment boundary won't be found by either mode.

# What this tool is NOT for — these belong to Script

- **Transcript-based editing**: any edit where transcript text or meaning decides what plays belongs to Script. Examples: clip/highlight extraction, "cut slices", "keep the part about X", "make a short version", delete / restore / move / copy / reorder / final cut.
- **Selecting / inserting transcript content into the timeline**: Script. `read_script` materializes `library/<filename>.md` (full transcripts); copy lines into `timeline.md`, then `apply_script()`.
- **Cutting speech from a timestamp**: use this tool only to identify the spoken text/range, then go back to Script. Do not use the returned frames with `split_item`, `edit_item`, or deletes to choose transcribed content.
- **Reading transcript text**: `timeline.md` (current cut) or `library/<filename>.md` (full source) after `read_script`.

# After matching

Use the timeline frames with marker / B-roll / overlay tools at the matched moment. If the user's goal is to cut, keep, extract, remove, or reorder what is spoken there, use the match only as orientation, then edit `timeline.md` with Script and `apply_script`. Do NOT drive `split_item`, `edit_item`, or item deletes from this output to select transcript content.

# Timestamps live here, not in Script

find_transcript is the **single source** of timestamps. Script markdown (`library/*.md`, `timeline.md` from `read_script`) contains sentence text only — **no word-level or segment-level timing**. If find_transcript returns 0 matches for a phrase you can see in Script, the phrase isn't on the active timeline (edited out, or in an asset not used here). Don't open Script to look for timestamps — it won't help.

# Per-word timestamps (opt-in)

Pass `includeWordTimestamps: true` when you need timing for **each word inside the matched phrase** — e.g. syncing MG animation beats to which word is being spoken, or driving karaoke-style highlights. Adds a `Words:` block under each match. Skip it for the typical single-phrase anchoring case (extra output costs context tokens).

Use when syncing animation beats to speech cadence (e.g., MG internal rhythm matched to which word is being said). Adds a `Words:` block under each match with each word's start -> end time. Skip for the typical lookup case (anchoring a single overlay to a phrase boundary).

tools.name: isolate_voice
tools.description:
Apply or clear AI voice isolation (DeepFilterNet3 speech enhancement) on a video or audio item with spoken human voice. This is not generic denoise — it is speech-only enhancement.

IMPORTANT — only for clips that contain spoken human voice:
DeepFilterNet3 is a speech-enhancement model. It suppresses everything EXCEPT human speech. Applying it to a clip with no speech (music, ambient noise, sound effects, action footage) will distort or silence the audio. If the user's clip does not contain spoken voice, tell them ChatCut does not have a suitable tool for that request.

Use this tool for spoken-voice dereverb too:
When the user asks to reduce room echo, reverb, reverberation, or "echoey" / "distant" speech (去混响 / 回声大 / 空旷感 / 人声不贴耳), treat it as a voice-isolation use case if the target clip contains spoken human voice. Do not use it as generic dereverb for music, ambience, SFX, or non-speech recordings.

How this tool works:
- Preferred route when the editor is open: call action="apply" with itemId and sourceAssetId, no filePath. The open editor runs the same AI Voice Isolation pipeline as the manual UI, creates the derived audio asset, and points the item at it.
- Workspace route: run the `deep-filter` binary (DeepFilterNet3) locally to produce a voice-isolated WAV, then call action="apply" with filePath and sourceAssetId. The local engine MUST be DeepFilterNet3, or the derivative is incompatible with the editor's cache.
- External connector route: call import_media action="create_session", run the asset-import upload-media.mjs helper on the already-cleaned WAV, then action="attach" with the returned audio assetId. The source asset is never modified; clearing reverts to the original.

If DeepFilterNet3 is missing, install it; do not substitute generic ffmpeg denoise. Use a `deep-filter` release binary, or a temp Python 3.11 venv with `deepfilternet==0.5.6`, `torch==2.3.1`, `torchaudio==2.3.1`, `soundfile==0.12.1`; run `deep-filter-py --model-base-dir DeepFilterNet3 --atten-lim <0-100> --output-dir <dir> <input.wav>`.

Workspace workflow (driven by the `voice-isolation` skill when the frontend route is unavailable):
1. read_project to find the target item (prefix id is fine) and its assetId. If it shows no speech signals and likely has no spoken voice, do NOT proceed — tell the user.
2. Get the full source asset audio locally, not just the visible timeline range; timeline items can have sourceStart offsets. For video, extract the full audio track with ffmpeg and transcode to mono 48 kHz WAV.
3. Run DeepFilterNet3 on that full-source WAV: `deep-filter -a <0-100> <input.wav>` or `deep-filter-py --model-base-dir DeepFilterNet3 --atten-lim <0-100> --output-dir <dir> <input.wav>` (atten-lim-db: 0=no reduction, 100=full).
4. apply (workspace filePath) or attach (already-uploaded denoisedAssetId).

itemId / sourceAssetId / denoisedAssetId accept 10-hex prefix ids or full UUIDs.

Actions:
- apply: itemId, sourceAssetId (the item's current assetId), optional strength (0-100, default 100). With no filePath, asks the open editor to run AI Voice Isolation. With filePath, uploads the workspace wav and points the item at it; strength must match the deep-filter -a value.
- attach: itemId, denoisedAssetId (an already-uploaded voice-isolated audio asset), sourceAssetId, optional strength. Points the item at that asset. On connectors with no workspace, import the cleaned WAV through import_media plus the asset-import upload-media.mjs helper, then attach its returned assetId.
- clear: itemId only. Reverts to the original audio.

Returns JSON describing what changed.

External MCP voice-isolation rule: prefer action="apply" without filePath when the project is open in the editor; ChatCut routes the request through the editor tool bridge so the browser runs the native AI Voice Isolation pipeline. If no editor is open, create a DeepFilterNet3 full-source WAV locally, call import_media action="create_session", run the asset-import upload-media.mjs helper on that WAV, then call action="attach" with the returned assetId as denoisedAssetId plus sourceAssetId and strength. Do not pass workspace filePath on this connector.
