tools.name: manage_design_style
tools.description:
Manage the user's library of Design Styles. A design style is the ONLY representation of brand identity in this product — the currently applied design style IS the project's design style. There is no separate "project-only" brand.

Actions split into two namespaces by storage:

# User library actions (DB-backed)
- list: show the current project's active design style, then all of the user's saved design styles.
- get: show the full designSpec for the current project's active design style. Pass designStyleId to inspect a specific saved design style or catalog preset.
- create: make a new design style from a designSpec. **Auto-applies to the current project by default** — pass `applyToProject: false` if you only want to add it to the library without switching this project to it. Pass a clear name ("Acme", "{Client} · Winter campaign") — avoid generic names. **DO NOT use `create` to apply a catalog preset — use `apply_preset` instead, which avoids retyping the spec.**
- update: merge a patch into an existing design style's spec, rename it, and/or set its `thumbnailUrl` cover. By default targets the design style currently applied to this project; pass designStyleId to target a specific one. If the design style is used by >1 project, the tool returns a confirmation_required response (see below) — you MUST ask the user and, if they want to proceed, re-call with `confirmShared: true`. If they'd rather have a separate variant without affecting other projects, use the `create` action to make a new design style instead.
- apply: switch the current project to a different existing design style. Requires designStyleId.
- clear: remove the active design style from the current project without deleting saved user styles or catalog presets. Use this before validation runs that need to test first-run style alignment.
- delete: permanently remove a design style. Destructive — the tool returns confirmation_required on first call (see below); you MUST confirm with the user before re-calling with `confirm: true`. Deletion does NOT remove assets already used in existing projects — it just removes the design style from the library, so it can no longer be re-applied.

# Catalog actions (file-backed curated presets, read-only)
- list_presets: enumerate the curated catalog of design style presets (rows in design_style where ownerId IS NULL AND visibleInFrontend). Returns id (UUID) / name / thumbnail URL / applicable scenarios / description per preset — enough for host-specific widget-forms skills to render a visual picker, or for hosts without visual cards to present numbered choices. Does NOT return the persisted designSpec. Optional `scenario` arg filters by applicable scenario tag for recommendation / selection. The returned `description` is the main agent-facing style profile for matching presets to the user's requested visual direction. Optional `locale` arg returns localized name/description (pass the user's chat language: 'zh' / 'en' / 'es'; defaults to English). This is the single source of truth for "what styles can the user pick" — never hardcode an option list.
- apply_preset: pin the current project's active design style directly to a curated catalog preset. Pass only `presetId` (the UUID returned by list_presets). No clone is created — the project's `designStyleId` FK points at the catalog row itself. A user-owned copy is only forked later if the user actually edits the spec (handled in `update`). This is the correct path after the user picks a catalog design style from the picker. For MG/design work, call `get` after applying; `list_presets` names/descriptions are picker summaries, not the full designSpec.

# Confirmation protocol (update shared / delete)

When the tool needs user confirmation, the response starts with `status: "confirmation_required"`. Example outputs the sandbox script will surface:

```
This design style is used by 3 project(s). Editing it will affect every project using it. Ask the user to confirm, then call update again with `confirmShared: true` to proceed. If the user wants a separate variant instead, use the `create` action to make a new design style.
```

```
Deleting design style "Acme" is permanent and cannot be undone. It is still used by 2 project(s). After the user confirms, call delete again with `confirm: true`.
```

When you see either, STOP and ask the user. Don't silently re-call; don't silently proceed. Relay the situation faithfully and let the user decide.

# designSpec shape

`thumbnailUrl` is a Design Style UI cover for library / picker display only. It is not a generation reference. Use it when the user asks to set the Design Style cover, or when importing a style page with a clear preview image. Do not duplicate that same image in `images[]` unless it should also influence generation.

Every element has exactly one label field — `role` — that says **what it's for / how it's used**. Not what it looks like.

```json
{
  "colors": [
    { "role": "primary",    "value": "#6C5CE7" },
    { "role": "accent",     "value": "#A8E6CF" },
    { "role": "background", "value": "#FCFBF8" },
    { "role": "CTA button", "value": "#FF6B35" }
  ],
  "fonts": [
    { "role": "heading", "family": "Inter" },
    { "role": "body",    "family": "Inter" }
  ],
  "logos": [
    { "role": "wordmark",       "url": "https://..." },
    { "role": "icon",           "url": "https://..." },
    { "role": "dark-bg variant","url": "https://..." }
  ],
  "images": [
    { "role": "product hero",  "url": "https://..." },
    { "role": "team photo",    "url": "https://..." }
  ],
  "styleGuide": "Modern, technical, confident."
}
```

Field rules:
- **colors[]**: `value` hex (required). `role` says what the color is FOR. Recommended standard tokens: `primary`, `secondary`, `accent`, `background`, `text` — use these when they fit. If the design has a specific non-standard purpose, write it freely: `"CTA button"`, `"divider"`, `"error"`, `"Tiffany Blue"`. **Don't describe the hue** ("Warm Cream", "Near Black") — the hex + swatch already show that; role is noise if it restates the appearance.
- **fonts[]**: `family` (required, CSS font-family). `role` says what the font is FOR. Standard tokens: `heading`, `body`, `mono`. Or freeform: `"display"`, `"code"`, `"caption"`.
- **logos[]**: `url` required. `role` says which variant / when to use: `primary`, `icon`, `wordmark`, or freeform like `"dark-bg"`, `"watermark"`. **⚠️ On update, logos REPLACE the entire array** — to add one, first call `manage_design_style` with `action: "get"`, then send the full new array.
- **images[]**: `url` + `role` (required). `role` says what the image depicts / how to use it: `"product hero"`, `"team photo"`, `"scene reference"`, `"moodboard"`. Specific enough that downstream generators pick the right one per scene. **⚠️ Same REPLACE semantics as logos.**
- **styleGuide**: high-level design tone only — one-line identity like "Modern, technical, confident" or "Editorial, bold, high-contrast". On update, replaces (empty string clears). Two hard rules:
  - **Don't redescribe what other fields already show.** No "warm off-white backgrounds with near-black text", no "gradient blue-pink-orange logo", no "Inter heading and body". Those fields already carry that info.
  - **Don't invent design prescriptions.** No layouts, animation styles, typography weights. Visual generators degrade when given prescriptive design briefs.
  Only record abstract tone / voice / identity. When in doubt, keep it empty.

On update: colors/fonts merge by `role` (case-insensitive, whitespace-normalized) — patching `[{role:"primary", value:"#new"}]` updates only the primary, leaving others untouched. Logos/images/styleGuide replace.

Design style names are unique per user; server auto-appends " (2)", " (3)", etc. on collision — your call never fails on name conflict.

tools.name: manage_markers
tools.description:
Manage note markers on a timeline. Current contract: marker-note-v2. A marker is a point-or-range comment anchored to timeline frames — for example "fix audio dip here" or "this cut is too tight". Each marker has a frame position, optional duration, and one user-visible field: note.

Two marker scopes:
- **Ruler markers** (default, scope:"project"): anchored at an absolute timeline frame. Stay where they are when clips move or get edited. Use for section labels, act breaks, timeline-level reminders.
- **Clip markers** (scope:"item"): anchored to a specific clip via itemId. Travel with the clip across move, trim (either side), playback-rate change, split, and duplicate, staying glued to the same source moment. Use for clip-specific notes like "color grade this shot" or "tighten the cut here".

Use this tool to:
- list: show note markers on the active timeline (both scopes), or on timelineId when provided.
- get: fetch one marker by prefix id.
- create: drop a note marker. Pass itemId to make it a clip marker; omit to make it a ruler marker. Defaults: durationFrames=0 (point). fromFrame is always in timeline-frame coordinates — the tool converts internally when itemId is set.
- batch_create / bulk_create: drop multiple note markers in one call (each entry can target a different itemId or none).
- update: change an existing marker's fromFrame, durationFrames, and/or note.
- batch_update / bulk_update: update multiple existing markers in one call.
- delete: remove an existing marker by prefix id, or several at once via markerIds (batch_delete / bulk_delete are aliases) — one call for the whole cleanup, never one call per marker.
- transcript-backed notes: for exact transcript quotes, pass transcriptSegments plus optional notePrefix instead of free-text note. The tool copies transcript text and fills fromFrame from the first selected segment unless you pass fromFrame explicitly.

Choosing scope:
- "mark this clip" / "note on this shot" / "remember to fix this take" → clip marker (set itemId from read_project items).
- "section header at 0:30" / "act break" / "TODO at frame X" → ruler marker (omit itemId).
- When the user names or selects a specific clip, prefer clip marker.

Evidence-bound placements: when the user asks for a marker at a transcript/caption phrase, visual moment, current selection, or other evidence-derived location, create only after you have exact frame/timestamp evidence from the user or a current tool result. If lookup fails, report that no marker was placed; do not use frame 0 or any placeholder fallback unless the user explicitly asked for start-of-timeline.

Temporary/probe markers are still real project markers. If you create one for verification, delete it and list markers to prove cleanup before optional work or final answer.

By default markers are scoped to the active timeline. If the user names or identifies a non-active timeline, pass timelineId from manage_timelines list instead of switching active timelines. Results echo the target timeline and the resulting scope so you can verify placement without an extra list/read call. Only pass the schema fields for this tool: action, timelineId, fromFrame, itemId, optional durationFrames, markerId, markerIds, note, markers, updates, transcriptSegments, transcriptTrack, and notePrefix.

tools.name: manage_timelines
tools.description:
Manage the project's timelines (sequences). A project can hold multiple timelines; exactly one is "active" — it is what the user sees in the editor, and the default target for edits, timeline frame inspection, and exports.

Actions:
- list: all timelines and which is active.
- create: new timeline, born with a default video track and ready to receive items from the asset library. Composition inherits the active timeline; override with width/height or ratio ("16:9", "9:16", "1:1", "4:3", "3:4"). To create several timelines, pass them all in one call via timelines (an array of {name, ratio, width, height} entries).
- duplicate: full copy of timelineId — tracks, items, markers, captions including word-level edits. Its transcript script is immediately editable with read_script/apply_script.
- switch: make timelineId active. Applies immediately to your later tool calls this turn, and the user's editor view follows. A hidden timeline can't be made active — restore it first (update hidden=false).
- update: rename (name), change composition (width/height/ratio), and/or hide/restore (hidden) timelineId, defaulting to the active timeline. On size changes, fit controls how existing items adapt: "contain" keeps everything visible, "cover" fills the frame. Hiding keeps all data but removes the timeline's tab for everyone; hiding the active timeline moves everyone to the newest visible one.
- delete: remove timelineId, or several at once via timelineIds in one atomic call. Everyone viewing a deleted timeline lands on the newest remaining timeline. A project keeps at least one timeline.

create and duplicate activate the new timeline by default so subsequent edits land on it (batch create activates the last entry); pass activate=false to leave the current selection alone. Name collisions auto-suffix "(2)".
For composition size, use ratio presets OR explicit width/height. Redundant preset dimensions are accepted (e.g. ratio:"9:16", width:1080, height:1920), but custom dimensions must omit ratio.

Choosing a starting point: duplicate when the new timeline should start from existing content (cut-downs, versions, language variants — trim the copy via its script); create when building fresh from the asset library.

Returns JSON; timeline objects are {id, name, width, height, active, hidden}.

tools.name: manage_transcript
tools.description:
Manage source transcript fixes and translation variants. Finding timestamps remains in `find_transcript`. Captions only choose which transcript variant to display.

For ordinary user-facing requests like "turn on bilingual captions", "translate my captions to English", or "show Chinese + English subtitles", prefer `edit_captions` action `language_mode` instead. `language_mode` ensures the translation and updates caption sourceScope in one step. In those requests, `languageCode` / `targetLanguage` means the TRANSLATION TARGET language, not the original language: English original + Chinese/English captions means target `zh`, not `en`. This `manage_transcript` tool only prepares/inspects transcript variants; it does NOT make a translation visible in captions by itself.

# Actions

## fix
Correct ASR mistakes or speaker assignments in an asset's **source** transcript. This changes transcript truth only; it does not edit timeline playback or remove audible content.

Input fields: `asset` required; `content` required with FIX / SPEAKER commands; optional `preview`.

`content` command format, one command per line:
- `FIX [sN]: wordIdx -> "newText"` — replace one word. `[sN]` is the segment id exactly as shown in read_script's timeline.md / library files; `wordIdx` is the word's 0-based position within that segment. Example: segment `[s3] I'm Ben Atkins here` → `FIX [s3]: 2 -> "Adkins"`.
- `SPEAKER [sN]: name` or `SPEAKER [sN-sM]: name` — assign those segments to a speaker (created if missing). Example: `SPEAKER [s2-s6]: Alice`.
Timestamps and text-search forms (`FIX "old" -> "new"`) are NOT accepted. When unsure of wordIdx, run with `preview: true` first — it shows the old word each command would touch without writing.

To rename an existing diarized speaker label everywhere (e.g. "that's Jon, not John"), do not reassign segments — use `edit_project` action `speaker-update` with the speaker id from `read_project`.

## retry_transcription
Force-retry ASR for an audio/video asset after transcription is stuck, timed out, or failed. Input fields: `asset` required. External MCP agents that already hold prepared audio bytes may pass `audioBase64` plus `audioMimeType` and optional `audioFilename` / `audioStartTimestampSec`; ChatCut uploads that audio and uses it for the retry. This bypasses backend duplicate locks safely and starts a new fenced transcription run; it does not wait for completion. Before reading transcript/captions, call `track_progress` once with `target: "transcription"`, `action: "status"`, and the returned asset id. If it is non-terminal, check again only after the returned interval.

## translation_list / translation_read
Inspect original + translation transcript variants for a source scope. Pass `json` with exactly one scope: `assetId`, `itemId`, `trackId`, or `allSpoken:true`. `translation_read` can include `targetLanguage` to narrow one language.

## Scope window semantics
`itemId`, `trackId`, and `allSpoken` only translate the speech the timeline actually USES — the source-media window each item plays (its in/out trim), not the whole asset. So a 1-hour source with only a 1-minute clip on the timeline translates roughly that minute's sentences, picked at full sentence boundaries (never a half sentence). `assetId` is the explicit "translate the ENTIRE asset" escape hatch — use it when you deliberately want the whole source covered regardless of what's on the timeline.

## translation_ensure
Incremental + idempotent: translates only the in-window sentences that are missing OR stale (source edited since translation), and reuses the ones already translated and current — no LLM cost for those. Use this when you need to prepare/refresh a translation variant without changing what captions show. After a re-edit that ADDED new footage, run `edit_captions` `language_mode` for user-visible captions, or run `translation_ensure` only if you are explicitly managing transcript variants. The result reports `translatedUtteranceCount` (new/changed sentences translated this run) and `skippedExistingUtteranceCount` (already-current sentences reused).

## translation_create
Force-regenerate the in-window sentences for `targetLanguage`, overwriting their prior translation rows. Existing translations for sentences OUTSIDE this scope's window are left intact. Use when the user asks for a fresh translation of the current selection, or to redo a region you do not trust.

# Translation scope json examples
- `{"trackId":"V1","targetLanguage":"en"}` — only the speech V1's items keep
- `{"source":{"assetId":"<id>"},"targetLanguage":"es","sourceLanguage":"en"}` — the whole asset
- `{"allSpoken":true,"targetLanguage":"en"}` — every used window across the timeline

# Translation result
`translation_ensure` and `translation_create` return `captionVisibility.visibleInCaptions:false` plus `applyToCaptionSource` follow-up `edit_captions` action/json values. You MUST call one of those returned `edit_captions` actions before telling the user subtitles are translated/bilingual. Prefer `applyToCaptionSource.languageModeBilingual` for normal original+translation display, or `languageModeTranslationOnly` for translation-only captions. Advanced `source_set` / `source_add` variants are included for custom source arrangements. Do not invent a captions source shape and do not store translations in `display_text` or caption word overrides.

# Translation reliability
The model translates sentence-delimited transcript chunks naturally; the backend computes caption word rows locally for rendering. Silence markers are preserved locally. If a batch misses any sentence, the backend retries missing sentences one-by-one before writing rows. If any speech sentence is still missing after retry, the action fails as a full or partial translation failure; treat either as no usable translation write and retry once or narrow the scope.

action.description: One of: fix, retry_transcription, translation_create, translation_ensure, translation_list, translation_read

asset.description: For action=fix or retry_transcription: asset id/prefix.

audioBase64.description: For action=retry_transcription: optional prepared audio bytes as base64 or a data:audio/...;base64 URL. External MCP only; use when the asset has no remoteUrl or you already extracted audio.

audioFilename.description: For action=retry_transcription with audioBase64: optional filename, e.g. extracted-audio.wav.

tools.name: read_script
tools.description:
Script is the editing surface for transcript-based editing: use it whenever the spoken transcript or meaning decides what should play, be removed, be kept, or be reordered on the timeline.

This includes talking-head cleanup, retake selection, filler removal, highlight extraction, short-clip creation, transcript-based trimming, semantic restructuring, and pulling source transcript onto the timeline.

This tool materializes the current multi-track cut (`timeline.md`) and full source transcripts (`library/<filename>.md`). On surfaces with a workspace filesystem (ChatCut backend agent with a sandbox attached), the files appear on disk; read and edit them with `read_workspace_file` / `edit_workspace_file` / `write_workspace_file` in Codex plugin sessions, or the equivalent native `Read` / `Edit` / `Write` tools. On external surfaces without a workspace, `timeline.md` and the library docs are returned inline in the tool result; edit the `timelineMd` string with your own tools, then pass the full edited content back via `apply_script({timelineMd})`.

# When to use

Use this for any operation that uses transcript text or meaning to decide what plays:
- Delete a spoken word / filler / context-dependent verbal habit, e.g. `[s1] 过去~~呢~~一个月`
- Delete or compress a visible silence marker / breath pause
- Trim, restore, move, copy, reorder, or delete transcript segments
- Choose the best retake and remove failed attempts or semantic duplicates
- Make clips / highlights / a short version / several versions based on what the speaker says, e.g. "cut slices", "keep the part about pricing", "make a 30s version", "make three versions on one track", "remove the intro"
- Pull library transcript onto the timeline, including an initial transcript-driven cut

# When NOT to use

Not for: correcting ASR mistakes in the source transcript (`manage_transcript` action `fix`); non-transcript media or visual properties (B-roll / MG / overlays / effects / transitions / position changes, use `edit_item`); mechanical whole-track filler cleanup or batch silence compression/restoration (`clean_script`); source pixels or bounded source speech (`inspect_asset`); timestamp lookup for placing non-transcript objects (`find_transcript`); asset library browsing (`browse_assets`).

Do not use `find_transcript` + `split_item` / `edit_item` as a shortcut for transcript-based editing. `find_transcript` can orient you to a spoken moment, but the actual cut / keep / reorder decision must be expressed in `timeline.md` and committed with `apply_script`.

# Workspace files

- `timeline.md`: the current multi-track cut. Structure:
  - `## V1` / `## A2`: H2 track section (alias from track type + order).
  - `### IMG_4560.mp4`: H3 source region (6-hex `[shortId]` suffix on filename collision). **Preserve H3 text exactly**; apply maps H3 to asset by it.
  - Body rows under each H3:
    - `[sN] text`: playing transcript segment (source-local id; only re-transcription changes it). If the same source segment appears multiple times on the same track, timeline rows render as `[sN@1]`, `[sN@2]`, etc.; preserve that `@N` suffix when editing, moving, or deleting an existing occurrence. To create an extra replay, add a bare library `[sN]` row instead of duplicating a rendered `[sN@M]` row verbatim.
    - `[cN] Nf`: non-transcript clip from this source (frame duration).
    - `[gap Nf]`: empty timeline space between items on this track (no source playing). On the only visible video track, this renders as black video.
    - `@speakerName`: render-only speaker boundary (auto-derived on re-materialize; no need to maintain when reordering or copying lines).
    - `[silence=Ns]`: inter-word or inter-segment silence. **Appears only when `showSilence: true`**; by default the file renders without these markers.
  Body order on disk = playback order.

- `library/<filename>.md`: full source transcript per transcribed asset. Library files are NOT valid `timeline.md` files: they use `# filename` H1 headers and source-local rows only. To bring content on-timeline, preserve `timeline.md`'s top markers, keep/create a `## V1` track section plus `### <filename>` source regions, then copy `[sN]` rows from `library/*.md` under the matching `###` region. Do not paste or concatenate whole library files into `timeline.md`.

# Editing workflow

Edit loop: first call materializes the files (clean, no `~~...~~`) → read `timeline.md` (workspace tools, or the inline content returned by this tool on external surfaces) → edit `timeline.md` skeleton (prefer `Edit`; if rewriting, preserve the top `# Timeline`, `script-stamp`, `script-timeline`, and `<!-- script:body -->` marker) → `apply_script()` (workspace-backed surface) or `apply_script({timelineMd: "<edited>"})` (external). Apply re-materializes `timeline.md` clean; just read it again. **Re-call this tool ONLY to change `track` scope.**

Track scope: omit `track` for normal transcript editing; the tool picks the default speech track. Pass `track` only after `read_project` shows the exact timeline track alias/id you need. Do not pass `A1` just because the content is spoken audio; talking-head video transcripts usually live on `V1`, while `A1` only works when an actual audio track exists.

# How to edit `timeline.md`

Strike (`~~...~~`) marks source content to remove from playback:

  Drop words in a segment        [s5] keep ~~drop~~ keep
  Drop Chinese particle          [s1] 过去~~呢~~一个月
  Drop a whole row               delete the line, OR wrap it:
                                   ~~[s5] hello world~~
                                   ~~[c1] 30f~~
                                   ~~[gap 30f]~~
  Keep only the start/end        trim text from the beginning or end of a row
  Disambiguate text repeats      [s5] ~~anchor~~ wanted
  Reorder / move a row           move the line on disk in any order; apply re-derives all frames
  Replay / repeat a row          add a bare [sN] row from library, or duplicate a timeline row and remove @N only on the NEW copy; each copy is a SEPARATE play of that content. Sequence whole versions back-to-back on one track by repeating rows (no find_transcript/edit_item, no timestamps).

`[sN]` rows edit words that were actually spoken in the source. Do not rewrite the wording or add words the source never said. If you need to remove words from the middle of a row, keep the row text and wrap only the unwanted source text in `~~...~~`; do not skip over the middle words by rewriting the row.

For Chinese text, do not add spaces that are not in the source:
- Correct: `[s1] 过去~~呢~~一个月`
- Wrong: `[s1] 过去一个月` (skips the middle word without marking it)
- Wrong: `[s1] 过去 ~~呢~~ 一个月` (adds spaces the source does not contain)

# Expected timeline result

Script edits rebuild timeline clips from source ranges. If you only trim the start or end of a clip, the result may stay as one trimmed clip. If you delete or move content from the middle of a clip, the original continuous source range cannot remain one clip: apply will create new clips for the kept ranges before and after the removed/moved range.

Predict the clip structure before applying: each middle deletion or middle move creates additional clip boundaries. This is expected physical editing, not a failed or unsupported word deletion. Still perform the requested spoken-content edit when the user asks for it; if the new clip boundaries create visible jump cuts, handle them afterward with optional B-roll / visual cover.

Do not create a bare `[gap]` on the primary video track to add breathing room. For pacing, preserve or restore source silence with `[silence=...]` / `clean_script`; for visual transitions, cover the moment with B-roll, MG, a card, or another visible layer. A bare video-track gap is a black frame.

**View or cut a specific breath / pause (剪气口)**: pass `showSilence: true` only when you need to inspect or manually adjust a specific pause. Strike `~~[silence=0.8s]~~` to cut it, or rewrite `[silence=0.8s→0.2s]` to compress it. For batch silence adjustment across the track (compress or restore), use `clean_script`; hidden silence markers do not prevent clean_script from processing them internally.

# User-facing language

You MUST NOT explain edits to the user with internal addresses such as `[sN]`, `[cN]`, `[gap]`, word indices, clip ids, or segment ids. The user cannot see those addresses and will not understand what they mean. Use them only in thinking, file edits, and tool calls. In chat, describe edits with the actual spoken content, a short quote, or a plain-language description.

Hidden silence markers do not prevent batch pause cleanup: use `clean_script` for whole-track or bulk silence compression/restoration. Turn this on only when you need to inspect or manually adjust specific pause durations.

tools.name: split_item
tools.description:
Cut one or more timeline items at given frame positions. One call can split many items, each at one or many frames.

# When to use

Cut a clip into pieces while preserving its source mapping, fades, effects, transitions, and markers. Splitting **does not change which spoken content plays** — the same media bytes play end-to-end across the resulting pieces. The Script "hard rule" in `edit_item` does not apply here.

Use this for physical clip management: preparing a transition, isolating a piece for visual treatment, splitting around an effect boundary, or making manual timeline organization easier while the content still plays the same.

For trimming (shortening one edge), prefer `edit_item` updates on `durationInFrames` + the source-offset field. Use `split_item` when you actually need two or more pieces.

# When NOT to use

Do not use `split_item` for transcript-based editing: clipping/highlight extraction, "cut slices", "keep the part about X", deleting a sentence, removing a retake, or making a short version based on what the speaker says. Do not take frames from `find_transcript`, split at those frames, and delete pieces to select spoken content. Use Script instead: `read_script` → edit `timeline.md` → `apply_script`.

# Body shape

`{"splits": [{"id": "...", "atFrame": 90}, {"id": "...", "atFrames": [60, 120, 180]}]}`

Each entry:
- `id`: timeline item id (6-char prefix from `read_project` accepted).
- `atFrame`: single timeline-frame cut position.
- `atFrames`: multiple cut positions; the item is cut into N+1 pieces.

Both `atFrame` and `atFrames` accept timeline frames (not source seconds). All cut frames must lie strictly inside the item (`from < cut < from + durationInFrames`).

# What survives the cut

- **Source offset** — each piece keeps the correct `sourceStartFromInSeconds` slice of the source media, accounting for `playbackRate`.
- **Fades** — `fadeIn` / `audioFadeIn` stays on the first piece only; `fadeOut` / `audioFadeOut` stays on the last piece only. Middle pieces have all fades zeroed.
- **Effects** — item-bound effects on the original item are cloned onto every piece (new effect ids).
- **Transitions** — a transition where the original item was the outgoing side now points at the last piece; incoming-side transitions point at the first piece.
- **Track-bound effects** (zoom blocks): any zoom block straddling a cut splits at the cut point with ease-in/out re-anchored.
- **Markers** — clip markers move to whichever piece contains them; item-local markers have their `fromFrame` re-anchored.

# Constraints

- Cannot split `effect` or `transition` items. Use `edit_item` to delete those.
- A single `split_item` call may not list the same `id` twice. Combine cuts for one item into a single `atFrames` array.
- Locked tracks reject splits with a clear error.

# Return

`{"splits": [{"itemId": "<original prefix>", "type": "video", "newIds": ["<piece1>", "<piece2>", ...]}, ...]}`

The original item id is deleted after the call. Subsequent edits should reference the returned `newIds`.

# Examples

- Single cut on one item: `{"splits": [{"id": "abc123", "atFrame": 150}]}`
- Three cuts on one item (4 pieces): `{"splits": [{"id": "abc123", "atFrames": [60, 120, 180]}]}`
- Cut two different items in one call: `{"splits": [{"id": "abc123", "atFrame": 60}, {"id": "def456", "atFrames": [30, 90]}]}`

tools.name: track_export
tools.description:
Inspect cloud export/render jobs for the current project.

Use this after submit_export, or when the user asks about Export History progress. This reads ChatCut's durable render job rows and reconciles live Remotion progress through the backend; agents should not reason from raw bucketName/remotionRenderId values.
Internal agents should report status and point users to the editor Export History panel. External MCP runtimes expose the finished render downloadUrl for connector delivery. When a completed result has downloadUrl, deliver it using the host's normal download flow.

- action=status: return current status.
- action=wait: compatibility alias for one immediate status read. If the job is not terminal, check again after at least 10 seconds, not repeatedly in one turn.
- Pass renderIds from submit_export when available.
- If renderIds is omitted, latest defaults to true and returns the most recent matching render job for this project.
- Set latest=false to list recent matching render jobs so you can tell the user which exports are complete, still rendering, or failed.
- onlyActive=true narrows latest lookup to currently rendering jobs.

tools.name: track_progress
tools.description:
Manage long-running work in the editor.
- Use this when a step has already been started and you now need its current status, progress, completion, or submission params recorded with the job.
- target=generation (default): track job-backed tasks such as image/video/music/TTS generation by job ID. Supports action=status, wait, params.
- target=transcription: track transcript readiness on an asset by asset ID. Supports action=status, wait.
- target=upload: wait for user-uploaded assets to finish uploading (remoteUrl becomes available). Use only before byte-dependent work such as pull_asset, frame inspection, export/render, or other operations that need remoteUrl/media bytes; do not wait for upload just to place/edit a registered asset.
- Use track_export for submitted video/audio/cloud render jobs and export history status.
- Every call returns immediately after one status read. action=wait is a compatibility alias that also returns immediately and includes check-back guidance for non-terminal work.
- Non-terminal results include checkBackAfterSeconds. When the current task depends on completion, use your environment's sleep command (for example, Bash `sleep 30`) for at least that interval, then call action=status once. Allow at most one sleep-and-recheck cycle per turn; if it is still non-terminal, tell the user and stop. Never busy-poll. If the current task is not blocked, tell the user it is still running and stop immediately.

tools.name: view_timeline_frames
tools.description:
Render one or more timeline frames of the current project composition. Hosted connectors return each cloud-rendered frame as a separate temporary image link; workspace-backed hosts may return individual downloaded files or one stitched inline image.

When to use
- Verify what the timeline looks like at a specific frame before reporting an edit as done.
- Compare multiple frames in one call (up to 9). Hosted connectors return one labeled resource link per requested frame. Download the links into a temporary local folder when the host cannot inspect remote images directly, then inspect them individually or combine the local copies into a temporary contact sheet.
- Frame-specific visual claims need fresh evidence — call this for the exact frames you are about to talk about.

Inputs
- "frames": integer frame numbers (non-negative). Single frame is allowed. If a frame equals the composition duration boundary, it is rendered as the last visible frame.
- "timelineId" (optional): override the active timeline; defaults to the current one.

Output
- Hosted connectors: one temporary JPEG resource link per frame, rendered by Lambda. These links expire and are not project assets. The ChatCut gateway does not download or stitch them; the external agent may download them locally for visual inspection.
- Workspace-backed hosts: downloaded JPEG paths or one inline JPEG written under "timeline-frames/" inside the sandbox workspace. Returned frame/time metadata is authoritative for each file.
- JSON includes "renderedBy": "frontend" when an open editor tab rendered browser-local preview pixels, or "cloud" when the backend rendered export-like pixels.

Notes
- In the desktop app, frames are rendered by the subscribed desktop editor when it is available; do not describe them as cloud-rendered unless runtime metadata/logs explicitly say Lambda was used.
- These images are NOT in the user's project asset library. If the user asks to see / save them, use push_asset on the workspace file.

External MCP note: this connector has no frontend route, so renderedBy is always "cloud". The gateway path is metadata-only: it reads composition state from the database, invokes Lambda still renders, signs the private outputs, and returns links without acquiring media download, Sharp, stitch, or workspace workers. Each requested frame is returned as its own temporary Lambda image resource link. If your host cannot inspect signed remote images directly, use curl with the full shell-quoted URI to download each frame into a mktemp folder, then open the local files with the host image-reading tool individually or stitch the temporary copies into a contact sheet. You have not visually verified a frame until you inspect its pixels. Local-only media, browser-held blobs, and upload-in-progress assets must be uploaded/registered with cloud-readable URLs before this can prove the timeline.

tools.name: web_browser
tools.description:
Scrape a web page via Firecrawl. Runs on the backend MCP server, no sandbox needed.

Pass formats to choose what comes back:
- markdown (default): clean LLM-ready text
- html / rawHtml: cleaned vs. unmodified
- images: array of image URLs on the page
- links: array of hyperlink URLs
- branding: { logo, colors, typography, spacing } for brand kit extraction
- summary: AI-generated page summary
- screenshot: full-page (when fullPage=true) or viewport screenshot

Screenshot specifics:
- When format=screenshot is requested, Firecrawl returns a screenshot URL. Download it into your local workspace first. Backend agents import that file through asset-import + push_asset; hosted external MCP uses import_media. The backend does not fetch or register screenshot bytes.

Structured extraction:
- query: natural-language extraction prompt (Firecrawl picks the schema)
- schema: explicit JSON schema for exact field names/types

Other useful options: waitFor (ms to wait for page load), fullPage, country (geo-proxy code), actions (raw Firecrawl actions JSON for scroll/click/wait flows), execJs (JS to run before extraction).

External MCP web-browse rule: Firecrawl scraping and screenshot capture can use external provider quota. Screenshot results are remote URLs; download a selected screenshot into your own sandbox, then use import_media if it must become a project asset.

tools.name: notion-create-attachment
tools.description:
Create an attachment and upload it to Notion. Provide exactly one source: - content for small UTF-8 text artifacts such as HTML, Markdown, plain text, CSV, JSON, XML, CSS, YAML, TSV, calendar, GPX, or SVG files. - source_url for a file available at a direct, publicly reachable HTTPS URL. This supports binary files and temporary signed download URLs. Notion performs a metadata-only HEAD request when supported, followed by the GET request that downloads the file. The URL must not redirect, require cookies or request headers, or resolve to a private network address. The filename must use a supported extension. The optional content_type is a MIME type and must agree with the filename; omit it to infer the type from the extension. Inline content is limited to 200 KiB after UTF-8 encoding. URL downloads must complete within one minute and are limited to 5 MiB for free workspaces and 50 MiB for paid workspaces. For local files, larger files, URLs that redirect, or authenticated downloads requiring headers, use ntn files create or the Notion File Upload API instead. The response includes a markdown_source value. To place the uploaded file on a page, pass that source to create-pages or update-page. Attach it within one hour: unattached uploads remain temporary and are deleted after they expire. "HTML", "HTML block", "HTML artifact", and "HTML embed" all mean an HTML file placed with so Notion renders the sandboxed preview. Never place HTML in a code block or file block. Use for other files. 1. Create an HTML artifact: {"filename":"report.html","content":"

Report

"} 2. Create Markdown with an explicit MIME type: {"filename":"notes.md","content_type":"text/markdown","content":"# Notes Hello"} 3. Import a PDF from a signed URL: {"filename":"report.pdf","source_url":"https://storage.example.com/report.pdf?signature=..."}

Inline Notion-flavored Markdown for comment text. For exact syntax, read the MCP resource `notion://docs/enhanced-markdown-spec` through your MCP client's resource-reading interface. Do NOT pass this URI to the Notion `fetch` tool or any URL-fetching tool. Use only the Rich text types and Mentions syntax that comments support. Comments support inline formatting (bold, italic, strikethrough, underline, code, links), inline math using `$`Equation`$`, and user/page/database/date mention tags such as `<mention-date start="YYYY-MM-DD"/>`. Do not use UI shortcuts like `@today`, `@name`, `[[page]]`, or autocomplete-style emoji syntax; those are editor affordances, not markdown syntax. Mention tags must include a real `url` where required by the spec. Block-level Markdown such as headings, lists, tables, blockquotes, and fenced code blocks is stored as plain comment text rather than rendered as blocks. - `rich_text`: Array of rich text objects. For content targeting, use `selection_with_ellipsis` with ~10 chars from start and end: "# Section Ti...tle content" <example description="Page-level comment"> {"page_id": "uuid", "markdown": "Comment with **important** context."} </example> <example description="Comment on specific content"> {"page_id": "uuid", "selection_with_ellipsis": "# Meeting No...es heading", "markdown": "Comment on this section."} </example> <example description="Reply to discussion"> {"page_id": "uuid", "discussion_id": "discussion://pageId/blockId/discussionId", "markdown": "Reply with [context](https://example.com)."} </example>

page_id.description: The ID of the page to comment on (with or without dashes).

discussion_id.description: The ID or URL of an existing discussion to reply to (e.g., discussion://pageId/blockId/discussionId).

selection_with_ellipsis.description: Unique start and end snippet of the content to comment on. DO NOT provide the entire string. Instead, provide up to the first ~10 characters, an ellipsis, and then up to the last ~10 characters. Make sure you provide enough of the start and end snippet to uniquely identify the content. rich_text.description: An array of rich text objects that represent the content of the comment. Provide exactly one of rich_text or markdown.

end.description: The end date of the date object, if any.

time_zone.description: The time zone of the date object, if any. E.g. America/Los_Angeles, Europe/London, etc.

id.description: The ID of the page in the mention.
The ID of the database in the mention.
The ID of the custom emoji.

mention.description: Mention objects represent an inline mention of a database, date, link preview mention, page, template mention, or user. A mention is created in the Notion UI when a user types `@` followed by the name of the reference.

tools.name: notion-create-database
tools.description: Creates a new Notion database using SQL DDL syntax, or a typed database using Notion's canonical schema for tasks, projects, or skills. Provide exactly one of: - schema: a CREATE TABLE statement. If no title property is provided, "Name" is auto-added. - database_type: one of tasks, projects, or skills. The database is created with the canonical required properties and typed metadata used by Notion. Returns Markdown with schema, SQLite definition, and data source ID in <data-source> tag for use with update_data_source and query_data_sources tools. Type syntax: - Simple: TITLE, RICH_TEXT, DATE, PEOPLE, CHECKBOX, URL, EMAIL, PHONE_NUMBER, STATUS, FILES - SELECT('opt':color, ...) / MULTI_SELECT('opt':color, ...) - NUMBER [FORMAT 'dollar'] / FORMULA('expression') - RELATION('data_source_id') — one-way relation - RELATION('data_source_id', DUAL) — two-way relation - RELATION('data_source_id', DUAL 'synced_name') — two-way with synced property name - RELATION('data_source_id', DUAL 'synced_name' 'synced_id') — two-way with synced name and ID (for self-relations) - ROLLUP('rel_prop', 'target_prop', 'function') - UNIQUE_ID [PREFIX 'X'] / CREATED_TIME / LAST_EDITED_TIME - Any column: COMMENT 'description text' Colors: default, gray, brown, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple, pink, red <example description="Minimal">{"schema": "CREATE TABLE ("Name" TITLE)"}</example> <example description="Tasks">{"database_type": "tasks", "title": "Tasks"}</example> <example description="With parent and options">{"parent": {"page_id": "f336d0bc-b841-465b-8045-024475c079dd"}, "title": "Projects", "schema": "CREATE TABLE ("Name" TITLE, "Budget" NUMBER FORMAT 'dollar', "Tags" MULTI_SELECT('eng':blue, 'design':pink), "Task ID" UNIQUE_ID PREFIX 'PRJ')"}</example> <example description="Self-relation (two-step: create database first, then use its data source ID with update_data_source to add self-relations)">{"title": "Tasks", "schema": "CREATE TABLE ("Name" TITLE, "Parent" RELATION('ds_id', DUAL 'Children' 'children'), "Children" RELATION('ds_id', DUAL 'Parent' 'parent'))"}</example>

parent.description: The parent under which to create the new database. If omitted, the database will be created as a private page at the workspace level.

page_id.description: The ID of the parent page (with or without dashes), for example, 195de9221179449fab8075a27c979105

title.description: The title of the new database.

description.description: The description of the new database.

schema.description: SQL DDL CREATE TABLE statement defining the database schema. Cannot be combined with database_type. Column names must be double-quoted and type options use single quotes.

tools.name: notion-create-pages
tools.description: ## Overview Creates one or more Notion pages, with the specified properties and content. ## Parent All pages created with a single call to this tool will have the same parent. The parent can be a Notion page ("page_id") or data source ("data_source_id"). If the parent is omitted, the pages are created as standalone, workspace-level private pages, and the person that created them can organize them later as they see fit. If you have a database URL, ALWAYS pass it to the "fetch" tool first to get the schema and URLs of each data source under the database. You can't use the "database_id" parent type if the database has more than one data source, so you'll need to identify which "data_source_id" to use based on the situation and the results from the fetch tool (data source URLs look like collection://<data_source_id>). If you know the pages should be created under a data source, do NOT use the database ID or URL under the "page_id" parameter; "page_id" is only for regular, non-database pages. ## Content Notion page content is a string in Notion-flavored Markdown format. Don't include the page title at the top of the page's content. Only include it under "properties". **IMPORTANT**: For the complete Markdown specification, always first read the MCP resource `notion://docs/enhanced-markdown-spec` through your MCP client's resource-reading interface. Do NOT pass this URI to the Notion "fetch" tool or any URL-fetching tool. Do NOT guess or hallucinate Markdown syntax. This spec is also applicable to other tools like update-page and fetch. ## Properties Notion page properties are a JSON map of property names to SQLite values. When creating pages in a database: - Use the correct property names from the data source schema shown in the fetch tool results. - Always include a title property. Data sources always have exactly one title property, but it may not be named "title", so, again, rely on the fetched data source schema. For pages outside of a database: - The only allowed property is "title", which is the title of the page in inline markdown format. Always include a "title" property. **IMPORTANT**: Some property types require specific formats: - Date properties: Split into "date:{property}:start", "date:{property}:end" (optional), and "date:{property}:is_datetime" (0 or 1) - Place properties: Split into "place:{property}:name", "place:{property}:address", "place:{property}:latitude", "place:{property}:longitude", and "place:{property}:google_place_id" (optional) - Number properties: Use JavaScript numbers (not strings) - Checkbox properties: Use "__YES__" for checked, "__NO__" for unchecked - Relation properties: Use an array of related page URLs or page IDs, e.g. ["https://www.notion.so/26ab1f9f4c5f80b18d3bd10a6b1d2f4e", "26ab1f9f-4c5f-80b1-8d3b-d10a6b1d2f4e"] **Special property naming**: Properties named "id" or "url" (case insensitive) must be prefixed with "userDefined:" (e.g., "userDefined:URL", "userDefined:id") ## Templates When creating a page in a database, you can apply a template to pre-populate it with content and property values. Use the "fetch" tool on a database to see available templates in the <templates> section of each data source. When using a template: - Pass the template's ID as "template_id" in the page object. - Do NOT include "content" when using a template, as the template provides it. - You can still set "properties" alongside the template to override template defaults. - Template application is asynchronous. The page is created immediately but starts blank; the template content will appear shortly after. ## Icon and Cover Each page can optionally have an icon and a cover image. - "icon": An emoji character (e.g. "🚀"), a custom emoji by name (e.g. ":rocket_ship:"), or an external image URL. Use "none" to remove. Omit to leave unchanged. - "cover": An external image URL. Use "none" to remove. Omit to leave unchanged. ## Examples <example description="Create a page with an icon and cover"> { "pages": [ { "properties": {"title": "My Page"}, "icon": "🚀", "cover": "https://example.com/cover.jpg" } ] } </example> <example description="Create a page from a database template"> { "parent": {"data_source_id": "f336d0bc-b841-465b-8045-024475c079dd"}, "pages": [ { "template_id": "a5da15f6-b853-455d-8827-f906fb52db2b", "properties": { "Task Name": "New urgent bug" } } ] } </example> <example description="Create a standalone page with a title and content"> { "pages": [ { "properties": {"title": "Page title"}, "content": "# Section 1 {color="blue"} Section 1 content <details> <summary>Toggle block</summary> Hidden content inside toggle </details>" } ] } </example> <example description="Create a page under a database's data source"> { "parent": {"data_source_id": "f336d0bc-b841-465b-8045-024475c079dd"}, "pages": [ { "properties": { "Task Name": "Task 123", "Status": "In Progress", "Priority": 5, "Is Complete": "__YES__", "date:Due Date:start": "2024-12-25", "date:Due Date:is_datetime": 0 } } ] } </example> <example description="Create a page with an existing page as a parent"> { "parent": {"page_id": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890"}, "pages": [ { "properties": {"title": "Page title"}, "content": "# Section 1 Section 1 content # Section 2 Section 2 content" } ] } </example> ## Async support Set "allow_async" to true to opt into receiving an async task result when this create operation is accepted for background execution. If this field is omitted or false, the tool keeps the existing synchronous result shape.

properties.description: The properties of the new page, which is a JSON map of property names to SQLite values. For pages in a database, use the SQLite schema definition shown in <database>. For pages outside of a database, the only allowed property is "title", which is the title of the page and is automatically shown at the top of the page as a large heading.

content.description: The content of the new page, using Notion Markdown.

template_id.description: The ID of a template to apply to this page. When specified, do not provide 'content' as the template will provide it. Properties can still be set alongside the template. Get template IDs from the <templates> section in the fetch tool results.

icon.description: An emoji character (e.g. "🚀"), a custom emoji by name (e.g. ":rocket_ship:"), or an external image URL. Use "none" to explicitly set no icon. Omit to leave unchanged.

cover.description: An external image URL for the page cover. Use "none" to explicitly set no cover. Omit to leave unchanged.

parent.description: The parent under which the new pages will be created. This can be a page (page_id), a database page (database_id), or a data source/collection under a database (data_source_id). If omitted, the new pages will be created as private pages at the workspace level. Use data_source_id when you have a collection:// URL from the fetch tool.

page_id.description: The ID of the parent page (with or without dashes), for example, 195de9221179449fab8075a27c979105

database_id.description: The ID of the parent database (with or without dashes), for example, 195de9221179449fab8075a27c979105

data_source_id.description: The ID of the parent data source (collection), with or without dashes. For example, f336d0bc-b841-465b-8045-024475c079dd

allow_async.description: Set to true to opt into receiving an async_task result when this create operation is accepted for background execution. If omitted or false, the tool keeps the existing synchronous result shape.

tools.name: notion-create-view
tools.description: Create a new view on a Notion database. Exactly one of "database_id" or "parent_page_id" must be provided: - "database_id": add a new view tab to an existing database. - "parent_page_id": create an inline linked database view on a page that references the existing "data_source_id" (like the UI "/linked" command). The linked view block is appended to the end of the parent page. Use "fetch" first to get the database_id, parent_page_id, and data_source_id (from <data-source> tags in the response). The caller must have edit access to the database (or parent page) and access to the data source. Supported types: table, board, list, calendar, timeline, gallery, form, chart, map, dashboard. The optional "configure" param accepts a DSL for filters, sorts, grouping, and display options. See the notion://docs/view-dsl-spec resource for full syntax. Key directives: - FILTER "Property" = "value" — filter rows - SORT BY "Property" ASC — sort rows - GROUP BY "Property" — group by property (required for board views) - CALENDAR BY "Property" — date property (required for calendar views) - TIMELINE BY "Start" TO "End" — date range (required for timeline views) - MAP BY "Property" — location property (required for map views) - CHART column|bar|line|donut|number — chart type with optional AGGREGATE, COLOR, HEIGHT, SORT, STACK BY, CAPTION - FORM CLOSE|OPEN — close/open form submissions - FORM ANONYMOUS true|false — toggle anonymous submissions - FORM PERMISSIONS none|reader|editor — set submission permissions - SHOW "Prop1", "Prop2" — set visible properties - COVER "Property" — cover image property <example description="Table view on existing database">{"database_id": "abc123", "data_source_id": "def456", "name": "All Tasks", "type": "table"}</example> <example description="Board grouped by Status">{"database_id": "abc123", "data_source_id": "def456", "name": "Task Board", "type": "board", "configure": "GROUP BY "Status""}</example> <example description="Filtered + sorted table">{"database_id": "abc123", "data_source_id": "def456", "name": "Active", "type": "table", "configure": "FILTER "Status" = "In Progress"; SORT BY "Due Date" ASC"}</example> <example description="Calendar view">{"database_id": "abc123", "data_source_id": "def456", "name": "Calendar", "type": "calendar", "configure": "CALENDAR BY "Due Date""}</example> <example description="Dashboard">{"database_id": "abc123", "data_source_id": "def456", "name": "Overview", "type": "dashboard"}</example> <example description="Linked view on a page">{"parent_page_id": "ghi789", "data_source_id": "def456", "name": "Company tasks", "type": "table", "configure": "FILTER "Company" = "Acme""}</example>

data_source_id.description: The data source (collection) ID. Accepts a collection:// URI from <data-source> tags or a bare UUID.

name.description: The name of the view.

database_id.description: The database to add a view tab to. Accepts a Notion URL or a bare UUID. Mutually exclusive with `parent_page_id`; exactly one must be provided.

parent_page_id.description: A page to create an inline linked database view on. Accepts a Notion URL or a bare UUID. The new linked view block is appended at the end of the page and references `data_source_id`. Mutually exclusive with `database_id`; exactly one must be provided.

configure.description: View configuration DSL string. Supports FILTER, SORT BY, GROUP BY, CALENDAR BY, TIMELINE BY, MAP BY, CHART, FORM, SHOW, HIDE, COVER, WRAP CELLS, and FREEZE COLUMNS directives. See notion://docs/view-dsl-spec.

tools.name: notion-download-attachment
tools.description: Download the contents of a small UTF-8 text attachment created by the Notion MCP `create-attachment` tool. Pass the `file_upload_id` returned by `create-attachment`. The attachment must belong to the requesting integration, have completed uploading, and use a supported text format such as HTML, Markdown, plain text, CSV, JSON, XML, CSS, YAML, TSV, calendar, GPX, or SVG. The response contains the complete text in `content` so you can save it locally, edit it, and call `create-attachment` again to upload a new version. Downloads are limited to 200 KiB. This tool does not fetch arbitrary URLs or return binary files. For larger or binary attachments, use the signed file URL returned when reading the containing Notion page. <examples> 1. Download a text attachment: {"file_upload_id":"12345678-90ab-cdef-1234-567890abcdef"} </examples>

file_upload_id.description: The FileUpload ID returned by the create-attachment tool.

tools.name: notion-duplicate-page
tools.description: Duplicate a Notion page. The page must be within the current workspace, and you must have permission to access it. The duplication completes asynchronously, so do not rely on the new page identified by the returned ID or URL to be populated immediately. Let the user know that the duplication is in progress and that they can check back later using the 'fetch' tool or by clicking the returned URL and viewing it in the Notion app.

page_id.description: The ID of the page to duplicate. This is a v4 UUID, with or without dashes, and can be parsed from a Notion page URL.

tools.name: notion-fetch
tools.description: Retrieves details about a Notion entity (page, database, or data source) by URL or ID. Provide URL or ID in `id` parameter. Make multiple calls to fetch multiple entities. Pages use enhanced Markdown format. For the complete specification, read the MCP resource `notion://docs/enhanced-markdown-spec` through your MCP client's resource-reading interface. Do not pass this URI to the Notion `fetch` tool or any URL-fetching tool. Databases return all data sources (collections). Each data source has a unique ID shown in `<data-source url="collection://...">` tags. You can pass a data source ID directly to this tool to fetch details about that specific data source, including its schema and properties. Use data source IDs with update_data_source and query_data_sources tools. Multi-source databases (e.g., with linked sources) will show multiple data sources. Set `include_discussions` to true to see discussion counts and inline discussion markers that correlate with the `get_comments` tool. The page output will include a `<page-discussions>` summary tag with discussion count, preview snippets, and `discussion://` URLs that match the discussion IDs returned by `get_comments`. Pass the special id `"self"` to get the connected workspace and user identity instead of an entity. The result includes a `self` object with the workspace id + name and the authenticated user's id, name, and email. Use this to label the connection (e.g. by workspace name) or obtain a stable id for the connected workspace and user. On MCP and RunTool surfaces, `self` also includes `current_tool_access`: a map from tool names to `available`, `limited_free_trial`, `upgrade_required`, or `not_enabled`. Entries include an `upgrade_url` when a workspace upgrade can change the status. Use this map to avoid calls that would only return an upgrade prompt. <example>{"id": "https://notion.so/workspace/Page-a1b2c3d4e5f67890"}</example> <example>{"id": "12345678-90ab-cdef-1234-567890abcdef"}</example> <example>{"id": "https://myspace.notion.site/Page-Title-abc123def456"}</example> <example>{"id": "page-uuid", "include_discussions": true}</example> <example>{"id": "collection://12345678-90ab-cdef-1234-567890abcdef"}</example> <example>{"id": "self"}</example>

id.description: The ID or URL of the Notion page, database, or data source to fetch. Supports notion.so URLs, Notion Sites URLs (*.notion.site), raw UUIDs, and data source URLs (collection://...). Pass "self" to fetch the connected workspace and user identity.

include_transcript.description: Whether to include meeting note transcripts. Defaults to false. When true, full transcripts are included; when false, a placeholder with the meeting note URL is shown instead.

include_discussions.description: Whether to include discussion/comment indicators in the page output. When true, adds a <page-discussions> summary with discussion count, preview snippets, and discussion:// URLs. Use with the get_comments tool to retrieve full discussion content. Defaults to false.

tools.name: notion-get-async-task
tools.description: Retrieves the current status of an async task that was started by another tool (for example, "create_pages" called with "allow_async": true). The status is one of "queued", "running", "retrying", "succeeded", or "failed". When the task has succeeded, the operation's result is included; when it has failed, an error is included instead. Poll this tool with the "task_id" from the original tool's "async_task" response. Wait briefly between polls — the original response includes a suggested backoff. <examples> 1. Check a task's status: {"task_id": "task_abc123"} </examples>

task_id.description: The ID of the async task to retrieve, as returned in the async_task response of the tool that started it.

tools.name: notion-get-comments
tools.description: Get comments and discussions from a Notion page. Returns discussions with full comment content in XML format. By default, returns page-level discussions only. Tip: Use the `fetch` tool with `include_discussions: true` first to see where discussions are anchored in the page content, then use this tool to retrieve full discussion threads. The `discussion://` URLs in the fetch output match the discussion IDs returned here. Parameters: - `include_all_blocks`: Include discussions on child blocks (default: false) - `include_resolved`: Include resolved discussions (default: false) - `discussion_id`: Fetch a specific discussion by ID or URL <example>{"page_id": "page-uuid"}</example> <example>{"page_id": "page-uuid", "include_all_blocks": true}</example> <example>{"page_id": "page-uuid", "discussion_id": "discussion://pageId/blockId/discussionId"}</example>

include_resolved.description: Include resolved discussions in the response. Defaults to false.

include_all_blocks.description: Include discussions on child blocks, not just page-level discussions. Defaults to false.

discussion_id.description: Fetch a specific discussion by ID or discussion URL (e.g., discussion://pageId/blockId/discussionId).

tools.name: notion-get-teams
tools.description: Retrieves a list of teams (teamspaces) in the current workspace. Shows which teams exist, user membership status, IDs, names, and roles. Teams are returned split by membership status and limited to a maximum of 10 results. <examples> 1. List all teams (up to the limit of each type): {} 2. Search for teams by name: {"query": "engineering"} 3. Find a specific team: {"query": "Product Design"} </examples>

query.description: Optional search query to filter teams by name (case-insensitive).

tools.name: notion-get-users
tools.description: Retrieves a list of users in the current workspace. Shows workspace members and guests with their IDs, names, emails (if available), and types (person or bot). Supports cursor-based pagination to iterate through all users in the workspace. <examples> 1. List all users (first page): {} 2. Search for users by name or email: {"query": "john"} 3. Get next page of results: {"start_cursor": "abc123"} 4. Set custom page size: {"page_size": 20} 5. Fetch a specific user by ID: {"user_id": "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000"} 6. Fetch the current user: {"user_id": "self"} </examples>

query.description: Optional search query to filter users by name or email (case-insensitive).

start_cursor.description: Cursor for pagination. Use the next_cursor value from the previous response to get the next page.

page_size.description: Number of users to return per page (default: 100, max: 100).

user_id.description: Return only the user matching this ID. Pass "self" to fetch the current user.

tools.name: notion-move-pages
tools.description: Move one or more Notion pages or databases to a new parent.

page_or_database_ids.description: An array of up to 100 page or database IDs to move. IDs are v4 UUIDs and can be supplied with or without dashes (e.g. extracted from a <page> or <database> URL given by the "search" or "fetch" tool). Data Sources under Databases can't be moved individually.

new_parent.description: The new parent under which the pages will be moved. This can be a page, the workspace, a database, or a specific data source under a database when there are multiple. Moving pages to the workspace level adds them as private pages and should rarely be used.

page_id.description: The ID of the parent page (with or without dashes), for example, 195de9221179449fab8075a27c979105

database_id.description: The ID of the parent database (with or without dashes), for example, 195de9221179449fab8075a27c979105

data_source_id.description: The ID of the parent data source (collection), with or without dashes. For example, f336d0bc-b841-465b-8045-024475c079dd

tools.name: notion-query-data-sources
tools.description: Query data from Notion databases using SQL or by specifying a view. By default, uses SQL mode to execute SQLite queries against one or more data sources. Alternatively, use view mode to execute a database view's existing filters and sorts. Archive selection is supported in view mode only. SQL mode does not accept "is_archived"; SQL archive support is a separate infrastructure follow-up. Limits: Single-data-source SQL queries have an hourly rate limit on Free and Plus plans. Queries across multiple data sources require an Enterprise plan with Notion AI. Prerequisites: 1. Use the "fetch" tool first to get database schema and data source URLs 2. Data source URLs are found in <data-source url="..."> tags in fetch results SQL mode (default): Execute custom SQLite queries against one or more data sources. - Use data source URLs as table names in your query - Supports parameterized queries for security - Checkbox values: use "__YES__" for checked, "__NO__" for unchecked Examples: 1. Simple query without explicit mode (defaults to SQL): { "data": { "data_source_urls": ["collection://f336d0bc-b841-465b-8045-024475c079dd"], "query": "SELECT * FROM "collection://f336d0bc-b841-465b-8045-024475c079dd" LIMIT 10" } } 2. Query with parameters: { "data": { "mode": "sql", "data_source_urls": ["collection://abc123"], "query": "SELECT * FROM "collection://abc123" WHERE Status = ? AND Priority = ?", "params": ["In Progress", "High"] } } 3. Query checkboxes: { "data": { "data_source_urls": ["collection://def456"], "query": "SELECT * FROM "collection://def456" WHERE Completed = ?", "params": ["__YES__"] } } View mode: Execute a specific database view's query with its filters and sorts. Omit "is_archived" or set it to false for non-archived rows. Set "is_archived": true to apply the view inside the archived partition. When the response has "has_more": true, pass its "next_cursor" as "start_cursor" in a follow-up view-mode request with the same "is_archived" value. Example: { "data": { "mode": "view", "view_url": "https://www.notion.so/workspace/Tasks-DB-abc123?v=def456", "is_archived": false } } Common use cases: - Aggregate data across databases - Filter records by complex conditions - Export data for analysis - Validate data quality - Generate reports from database content

data.description: The data required for querying data sources

data_source_urls.description: Notion data source URLs whose SQLite tables are available to the query; each data source is exposed as a table named by its URL. Obtain them from the fetch tool, in the format: collection://f336d0bc-b841-465b-8045-024475c079dd

query.description: Read-only SQLite query to execute against the data sources. Use a data source URL as the table name, e.g. SELECT * FROM "collection://..." WHERE .... Include every needed filter in WHERE (filters on views of the data source are not automatically applied). For time comparisons or ordering, normalize text timestamps with datetime(...) or date(...).

params.description: Positional parameters bound to `?` placeholders in the query. Prefer parameterized queries over string interpolation. Use "__YES__" for checked checkboxes and "__NO__" for unchecked checkboxes.

view_url.description: URL of a specific database view to query. Example: https://www.notion.so/workspace/db-id?v=view-id

start_cursor.description: Cursor for pagination. Use the next_cursor value from the previous response to get the next page.

page_size.description: Number of rows to return per page (default: 100, max: 100).

is_archived.description: Optional archive selector. Omitted or false queries non-archived rows only; true queries archived rows only.

tools.name: notion-query-database-view
tools.description: Query data from a Notion database view. Executes a database view's existing filters, sorts, and column selections to return matching pages. Use this to query a view exactly as configured. For custom SQL queries, aggregation, or querying across multiple data sources, use query_data_sources instead. By default, it returns non-archived rows only. Set "is_archived": true to query archived rows only. Prerequisites: 1. Use the "fetch" tool first to get the database and its view URLs 2. View URLs are found in database responses, typically in the format: https://www.notion.so/workspace/db-id?v=view-id Example: { "view_url": "https://www.notion.so/workspace/Tasks-DB-abc123?v=def456", "is_archived": false } When the response has "has_more": true, pass its "next_cursor" as "start_cursor" in a follow-up request with the same "is_archived" value. Common use cases: - Query databases using pre-defined views (filters/sorts already configured), e.g. look for all tickets marked "In Progress" in a Tasks DB - Export filtered data for analysis - Generate reports from database content

view_url.description: URL of a specific database view to query. Example: https://www.notion.so/workspace/db-id?v=view-id

start_cursor.description: Cursor for pagination. Use the next_cursor value from the previous response to get the next page.

page_size.description: Number of rows to return per page (default: 100, max: 100).

is_archived.description: Optional archive selector. Omitted or false queries non-archived rows only; true queries archived rows only.

tools.name: notion-query-meeting-notes
tools.description: Query the current user's meeting notes data source. Applies a filter over meeting note properties. Title keyword searching is done via filter on property "title" (e.g. string_contains). Title keyword matching is case-insensitive; capitalization does not matter. Returns up to 50 rows of matching meeting notes. Prerequisites: 1. Use the "search" tool to find people IDs if you need to filter by attendees Query building: - Ignore terms semantically related to meeting outputs (e.g. "summaries", "notes", "todos", "action items", "deliverables"). These signal the user wants outcomes from their meetings, not a title filter. - For example, "what are my meeting todos?" means filter meetings and find action items — do NOT add a title filter for "todos". - Only add a title filter when confident the user is targeting a specific meeting title (e.g. "standup", "sprint planning", "1:1 with Alice"). - Generic date phrases like "recent meetings", "latest meetings", "meetings this week", or "yesterday's meetings" should be interpreted as date range filters — never as title filters. - If a filter returns no results, simplify to a single term. The system is lexical, so multi-word title filters may not match. - Unless a user explicitly asks about a meeting titled with another user's name, assume they're referring to attendees or creators. Only add a title filter with a person's name as a fallback if attendee filtering returns no results. Default behavior: - This tool by default returns meeting notes where the current user is an attendee or creator. There is no need to add a filter for the current user. Filterable properties: - "title" (text) — meeting title - "notion://meeting_notes/attendees" (person) — meeting attendees - "created_time" (date) — when the meeting note was created - "created_by" (person) — who created the meeting note - "last_edited_time" (date) — when the meeting note was last edited - "last_edited_by" (person) — who last edited the meeting note Combinator filters use "filters" (not "operands"): { "operator": "and" | "or", "filters": [ ... ] } Date filtering (recommended default: date_is_within): - Prefer "date_is_within" for relative windows like "past N days/weeks/months". - Relative (common): { type: "relative", value: "the_past_week" | "the_past_month" | "this_week" } - Relative (custom): { type: "relative", value: "custom", direction: "past" | "future", unit: "day" | "week" | "month" | "year", count: <number> } - Exact range: { type: "exact", value: { type: "daterange", start_date: "YYYY-MM-DD", end_date: "YYYY-MM-DD" } } - Single-date operators ("date_is", "date_is_before", "date_is_after", "date_is_on_or_before", "date_is_on_or_after"): - Exact: { type: "exact", value: { type: "date", start_date: "YYYY-MM-DD" } } - Relative shortcuts: today | tomorrow | yesterday | one_week_ago | one_week_from_now | one_month_ago | one_month_from_now Title keyword filtering (OR vs AND): - Use OR ("operator": "or") when unsure or for broad discovery. - Use AND ("operator": "and") when the user is specific and you want to narrow results. - Break multi-word phrases into individual terms and filter on each term separately. Example 1: Filter meetings from the past week (relative): { "filter": { "operator": "and", "filters": [ { "property": "created_time", "filter": { "operator": "date_is_within", "value": { "type": "relative", "value": "the_past_week" } } } ] } } Example 2: Filter meetings from the past 3 days (custom relative): { "filter": { "operator": "and", "filters": [ { "property": "created_time", "filter": { "operator": "date_is_within", "value": { "type": "relative", "value": "custom", "direction": "past", "unit": "day", "count": 3 } } } ] } } Example 3: Filter meetings by exact date range: { "filter": { "operator": "and", "filters": [ { "property": "created_time", "filter": { "operator": "date_is_within", "value": { "type": "exact", "value": { "type": "daterange", "start_date": "2025-01-01", "end_date": "2025-12-31" } } } } ] } } Example 4: Filter meetings created after a specific date: { "filter": { "operator": "and", "filters": [ { "property": "created_time", "filter": { "operator": "date_is_after", "value": { "type": "exact", "value": { "type": "date", "start_date": "2025-06-01" } } } } ] } } Example 5: Filter meetings by a specific attendee (use "search" tool first to get user ID): { "filter": { "operator": "and", "filters": [ { "property": "notion://meeting_notes/attendees", "filter": { "operator": "person_contains", "value": [ { "type": "exact", "value": { "table": "notion_user", "id": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890" } } ] } } ] } } Example 6: Combine attendees with date range: { "filter": { "operator": "and", "filters": [ { "property": "created_time", "filter": { "operator": "date_is_on_or_after", "value": { "type": "exact", "value": { "type": "date", "start_date": "2025-01-01" } } } }, { "property": "created_time", "filter": { "operator": "date_is_on_or_before", "value": { "type": "exact", "value": { "type": "date", "start_date": "2025-01-31" } } } }, { "property": "notion://meeting_notes/attendees", "filter": { "operator": "person_contains", "value": [ { "type": "exact", "value": { "table": "notion_user", "id": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890" } } ] } } ] } } Example 7: Filter meetings by title content: { "filter": { "operator": "and", "filters": [ { "property": "title", "filter": { "operator": "string_contains", "value": { "type": "exact", "value": "design review" } } } ] } } Example 8: Filter meetings matching any of several title terms (using "or"): { "filter": { "operator": "or", "filters": [ { "property": "title", "filter": { "operator": "string_contains", "value": { "type": "exact", "value": "standup" } } }, { "property": "title", "filter": { "operator": "string_contains", "value": { "type": "exact", "value": "sync" } } } ] } }
